details_text: HackSprint 3.0 — Build Bold. Ride Beyond. About the Event HackSprint 3.0 is a national-level, 36-hour hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, in collaboration with the Metaverse Association. HackSprint 3.0 brings together passionate developers, designers, problem-solvers, and innovators from across India to transform creative ideas into impactful, technology-driven solutions. It provides a platform to experiment with emerging technologies, collaborate with like-minded innovators, and tackle real-world challenges. Mode: Online Preliminary Round + Offline Final Round Final Venue: Karpagam Academy of Higher Education (KAHE), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu Final Hackathon Duration: 36 hours Application Deadline: 28 December 2026 PPT Submission Template: Will be announced soon! How It Works Round 1: Online Idea Submission & Screening The first round will be conducted online. Interested teams must submit a PowerPoint presentation (PPT) outlining their proposed project idea before the application deadline. The presentation should explain: Problem Statement: What real-world problem are you addressing? Proposed Solution: How will your idea solve the problem? Innovation: What makes your approach unique? Feasibility: How can the solution be implemented? Expected Impact: Who will benefit from your solution? Team Portfolio: Relevant projects, technical skills, and previous work, where available. The organizing team will evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and relevant portfolio experience. Following the evaluation, selected teams will be shortlisted for the final round. Important: Submitting an application does not guarantee participation in the final hackathon. Only shortlisted teams will be invited to the offline round. Round 2: Offline Final Hackathon Shortlisted teams will participate in the 36-hour offline hackathon at Karpagam Academy of Higher Education, Coimbatore. Participants will develop their proposed solutions, build prototypes, test their implementations, and present their projects to the judging panel. Final evaluation will focus on innovation, technical implementation, functionality, feasibility, problem-solving, and overall impact. Final-round dates will be announced once confirmed. HackSprint 3.0 Tracks 1. Agrotech Leverage technology to address agricultural challenges through smart irrigation, precision farming, AI-enabled agriculture, resource optimization, and sustainable farming solutions. 2. MedTech Develop technology-driven healthcare solutions focused on diagnostics, remote healthcare, medical accessibility, patient monitoring, and improved healthcare delivery. 3. EduTech Reimagine education through digital learning platforms, adaptive learning systems, skill-development tools, inclusive education, and innovative teaching technologies. 4. WildVisionTech Explore AI- and ML-powered solutions for wildlife conservation, anti-poaching intelligence, environmental monitoring, and biodiversity protection. 5. Open Innovation Think without boundaries. Build creative, technology-driven solutions to meaningful real-world problems across any domain. What Awaits You? An opportunity to showcase your creativity and technical skills. A platform to transform ideas into practical solutions. Collaboration with passionate developers, designers, and innovators. An opportunity to present your work and receive feedback from the judging panel. Recognition for outstanding innovation and problem-solving. Prize details, partners, and additional opportunities will be announced through official HackSprint 3.0 communication channels. Rules & Regulations Idea Submission: Teams must submit their project proposal as a PPT before the first-round deadline. Screening: Teams will be shortlisted based on their ideas and relevant portfolios. Final-Round Eligibility: Only shortlisted teams may part

title: Agents that act. Systems that answer. | Free Virtual Agentic-AI Hackathon
description: About the Hackathon: Anyone can build an AI demo that works once. Agents that act. Systems that answer. is about what happens when it goes wrong. It's a free, 3-day virtual hackathon for student builders, hosted by…
details_text: About the Hackathon: Anyone can build an AI demo that works once. Agents that act. Systems that answer. is about what happens when it goes wrong. It's a free, 3-day virtual hackathon for student builders, hosted by StudentChakra and co-hosted by Priyanshu Agarwal (founder of NextMove, organiser of Hackorizon). What You'll Build: An agentic AI system for a real person with a real task. Start with a person, not an industry: who are they, what do they hate doing, what does your agent do for them, and where does it break? Solo or in a team of up to 4. No experience required. How Projects Are Judged: We judge how your project behaves when things go wrong: Failure modes: how does it break? Human oversight: who stays in the loop? Intervention: can someone stop it? Reversibility: can a mistake be undone? Plus usefulness to a real person and the quality of your working build. Prizes: $680 in prizes: 1st place about $500 in Apify credits; 2nd and 3rd place Cursor subscriptions. Judges: Experts from AI governance, cybersecurity, venture and OpenAI, including Dr. Esona Fomuso (formerly VP of Technology, JPMorgan Chase), Dr. Aleem Khalid Alvi (Professor of Cybersecurity & Software Engineering, Sheridan College), Kunal Kapoor (Venture Continuity, Katha) and Priyanshu Agarwal (ChatGPT Lab, OpenAI India). Key Dates: Registration closes: Nov 27 Hackathon: Nov 28–30 (virtual) Final results: Dec 8 Who Can Join: Students worldwide, solo or in teams of 1–4. Free.

details_text: Overview 48-Hour Online AI Hackathon Organized by Frontend Arena | In collaboration with Adaption Event Dates: December 10–12, 2026 Format: Online Duration: 48 hours Team Size: 2–4 members About AI BuildFest 2026 AI BuildFest 2026 is a 48-hour online hackathon focused on building AI-powered solutions for real-world challenges. It brings together students, developers, and AI enthusiasts to explore how custom-trained AI models can be developed and applied to practical problems. Participants will work in teams to understand a challenge announced during the hackathon, prepare or generate a suitable dataset, train their own model using Adaption’s platform, and build a working solution that demonstrates its capabilities. The event emphasizes practical model development, problem-solving, experimentation, and the creation of useful AI applications. Hackathon Theme Own Your AI: Train a Model That Solves a Real Problem Participants will be challenged to build an AI solution in which a trained model plays a meaningful role in addressing a real-world problem. The official problem statements and challenge requirements will be announced to registered participants during the hackathon. Teams will then have the event period to understand the challenge, develop their approach, train a model, and implement their solution. Challenge Format AI BuildFest will follow a challenge-based format. No specific tracks or problem statements are being published in advance. Official problem statements will be revealed during the hackathon. Teams will select or be assigned a challenge according to the instructions announced by the organizers. The challenge will require participants to develop an AI-based solution using the Adaption platform. Detailed requirements, deliverables, and submission instructions will be communicated when the challenge is announced. Teams should be prepared to work with data, train a model, and demonstrate a functional solution within the 48-hour period. Required Use of Adaption Adaption is the technology partner for AI BuildFest. Teams must use Adaption’s platform as part of their model-development workflow. Dataset Preparation or Generation Teams will use Adaptive Data to transform raw files into a training dataset, or Invent-a-Dataset to generate a dataset suited to their challenge. Model Training Teams will use AutoScientist to train their own model for the selected task. Solution Development Teams will build a functional application or prototype that uses their trained model to address the announced challenge. Demonstration Teams must demonstrate their solution and explain how the dataset and trained model contribute to solving the problem. Participants retain their trained model weights and may publish them on platforms such as Hugging Face or Kaggle, subject to applicable platform terms and data or licensing restrictions. Core requirement: Projects must demonstrate meaningful use of Adaption for dataset preparation or generation and model training. Simply integrating an existing third-party AI API without training a model through the required Adaption workflow will not satisfy this requirement. Technical Workshop A technical workshop led by an Adaption representative is planned before the hackathon. It will help participants become familiar with the platform and its model-development workflow. details_text: Build with Agora — Bengaluru 2026 One Day. Real-Time AI. Real Builders. Voice-First Commerce: Reimagine shopping and customer experiences through natural voice interactions. details_text: Prompt to Product Website Registration All participants must register through the official Tech Habba platform using the link below. Tech Habba Website: https://tech-habba26.vercel.app/ About the Event Build, test, and deploy a functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) from a problem statement revealed at the event. Teams will use their technical skills, creativity, and approved AI tools to transform an idea into a working product within a limited timeframe. The focus is on solving the given problem effectively, demonstrating smart prompt engineering, building a usable product, and delivering a successful deployment. Team Formation: Teams must consist of 2–3 participants. Problem Statement: The problem statement will be released by the organizers at the beginning of the event. AI Tools: Approved AI tools may be used for prompting, development, testing, debugging, and deployment. Required Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptop and charger, along with their development tools, GitHub access, AI-tool accounts, and any required API credentials. Submission Requirements: Each team must submit: A publicly accessible live product URL. A GitHub repository containing the event project. Rules Original Work Only: All projects must be developed during the event in response to the released problem statement. Previously completed projects and project-specific code prepared before the event are prohibited. Approved AI Tools: Participants may use AI tools for prompting, coding, debugging, testing, and deployment, subject to the approved tools and restrictions specified by the organizers. Mandatory Submission: All required deliverables, including the live product URL, GitHub repository, README, prompt history, and screen-recorded demo, must be submitted before the deadline. Deployment: The submitted product must be publicly accessible and functional at the time of evaluation. Judging Criteria: Teams will be evaluated according to the following criteria: Problem-solving and innovation — 25% Prompt strategy and execution — 25% UI/UX and functionality — 20% Deployment and completeness — 15% Live pitch and demo — 10% Documentation — 5% Finalist Presentations: The top 8 teams must present a three-minute live demo, followed by two minutes of questions from the judges. Fair Play: Plagiarism, misrepresentation of work, and attempts to gain an unfair advantage are prohibited and may result in disqualification. Team Participation: All team members must be registered participants and contribute to the development and presentation of their solution. Submission Deadline: Late submissions may not be considered for ev

details_text: Continuum 2026 Hackathon is a two-round Open Innovation competition by NEXSUS at Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology (MMMUT), Gorakhpur. The hackathon invites student teams to identify meaningful real-world problems and develop innovative solutions that may be software-based, hardware-based, or hybrid/interdisciplinary . The competition consists of an online idea-submission round followed by an offline grand finale at MMMUT, Gorakhpur . Round 1 — Online Idea Submission Participants must submit either an Idea Abstract or Idea Presentation (PPT) explaining: Problem statement and relevance Proposed solution Innovation and originality Technical approach Feasibility Expected impact Scalability A completed prototype is not mandatory for Round 1. Round 2 — Offline Grand Finale Shortlisted Teams Will Report Physically at Mmmut, Gorakhpur For: Team Verification Orientation Preliminary Idea/technical Presentation Technical Interaction Verification of Existing/baseline Work The 12-Hour Build Sprint schedule Will Be Released Later. Teams Must Be Able to Explain, Defend, and Demonstrate Every Major Component of Their Solution. Copying Another Team's Solution or Submitting Someone Else's Code/product as One's Own Is Prohibited. Open-Source Libraries, Frameworks, APIs, Models, and Public Development Resources May Be Used Where Permitted, with Relevant Use Disclosed. Previously Developed Personal Components Must Also Be Disclosed. Hardware & Hybrid Projects Hardware and Hybrid Projects Are Welcome. Teams Will Be Evaluated Fairly on Demonstrated Engineering Progress. Working Subsystems, Circuits/prototypes, Simulations, Architecture, Integration Progress and Demonstrated Functionality May Be Considered Where a Fully Fabricated Product Is Not Feasible Within the 12-Hour Sprint. Final Submission Teams Must Provide: Project / Solution Title Concise Project Description Project Repository or Relevant Source/design Files Working Prototype or Demonstrable Implementation, Where Applicable Technology Stack Architecture / Implementation Summary Declaration of Major Pre-Existing, Open-Source and Ai-Assisted Components Final Presentation and Required Backup Demonstration Material Jury Evaluation Will Be Conducted by A Panel Comprising Industry Experts, Working Professionals, Domain Specialists and Experienced/senior Faculty Members . The Decision of The Authorized Jury and Organizing Committee Regarding Evaluation-Related Matters Shall Be Final. Who Should Participate? The Hackathon Is Designed for Student Teams interested in Solving Real-World Problems Through Technology, Innovation and Engineering. Projects Can Be Software, Hardware, Hybrid or Interdisciplinary. description: Overview DATANYX'26 is Telangana’s flagship 24-hour datathon, now in its third edition. It is organized by AWS Student Builder Group MJCET and IEEE SMC MJCET. It is a 24-hour event where you take raw data and turn it…
details_text: Overview DATANYX'26 is Telangana’s flagship 24-hour datathon, now in its third edition. It is organized by AWS Student Builder Group MJCET and IEEE SMC MJCET. It is a 24-hour event where you take raw data and turn it into a working prototype. You start from scratch. The problem statements, datasets are given to you on the first day. DATANYX started in 2024 as the first 24 hr datathon in Telangana. In 2025, it grew into a national event. This year, every problem is linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. So what you build can help solve real problems in the world. Domains: AgroTech (SDG 2, 12, 13, 15) EdTech (SDG 1, 4, 8) Urban Tech (SDG 6, 7, 9, 11) MedTech (SDG 3, 5, 10) Event Details: Dates: 28th and 29th November 2026 Venue: Ghulam Ahmed Hall, MJCET, Hyderabad Mode: Offline Event Structure: Phase 1 - Shortlisting Round (Online): In the first phase, teams are required to submit a unique problem statement of their own creation, accompanied by a solution abstract with a presentation that aligns with their selected domain. Teams must choose from one of the following domains: Med Tech, Urban Tech, Agro Tech or EdTech. The proposed presentation should reflect originality and innovation within the chosen domain.All submissions must be completed online on the provided PPT Template before the designated deadline. The DATANYX'26 PPT TEMPLATE & the DOMAIN DESCRIPTION are attached below . Phase 2 - Finals (MJCET): The top 15 teams from each domain will qualify for the final phase, held in person at MJCET, Hyderabad. Here, teams will be given a new problem statement revealed on the spot along with a sample dataset. They will then have 24 hours to brainstorm, design, implement, build, and submit their final solutions. This phase tests the teams' ability to think critically and collaborate effectively under pressure, turning ideas into impactful solutions within a limited timeframe. Shortlisted teams are required to pay a participation fee of ₹1000. Step 1: Getting Started: Click the Unstop link for Datanyx. Find the "Register" button and click it. Step 2: Sign In (Super Easy!): Choose your sign-in option: Google (fastest!) LinkedIn Email Enter your details: Phone number Email Wait for the OTP on your phone and enter it. Step 3: Your Basic Info: Fill in the following details: Your name School or workplace Course details Graduation date Country of residence Step 4: Team Formation: If you’re the Team Leader: Create your team: Choose a team name. Add teammates' emails. Remind them to check their email for the "View Opportunity" link. Watch for teammates' names to turn GREEN once they join! If you're joining someone’s team: Find the team name. Click "Send Request". Wait for the team leader to add you. Step 5: PPT Submission: Download the PPT template Create your PPT with the team Submit your PPT in the PPT  Submission box in PDF format . Step 6: Final Check: Find the "View Details" button. If it's GREEN = You’re all set! If it's RED = Someone still needs to confirm. Pro Tip: Make sure everyone confirms their participation—green names mean your team is ready! Judging: Teams are judged on accuracy, robustness, explainability, and how realistic their business plan is. Prizes: Rs 1,00,000 prize pool. Guidelines: Please follow the given format for the abstract PPT, or else your registration will be regarded as invalid. There is NO registration fee for the first round. The shortlisted teams (finalists) have to pay Rs. 1000 to confirm their participation in the second round. Cross year, cross specializations, and cross college teams are allowed. The Datathon is based on a 24-hour format. The timings for the Datanyx'26 are from 11 AM on the 28th of November to 11 AM on the 29th of November. Shortlisted teams are requested to travel to MJCET, Hyderabad, on their own; no travel allowances will be provided. Goodies will be provided to the shortlisted teams. details_text: About the Workshop Turn your game ideas into a fully playable game in this immersive 2-day offline workshop at IIT Bombay. The workshop is designed to provide hands-on experience, allowing participants to build and polish their own playable game prototype. Mode: Offline Venue: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Date: 15th & 16th December 2026 Duration: 12–16 Hours Format: Concept Sessions + Live Demos + Hands-On Practice + CTF Challenge Eligibility The workshop is open to participants interested in Game Development, Unity, AI, Game Design, or Interactive Technologies. No prior professional game development experience is required. Participants must register individually for the workshop. Participants must have access to a laptop/PC that meets the required specifications. Participants who fail to attend all required sessions will not be eligible for the certificate. Why Attend? Learn to build a playable game from scratch using Unity. Gain hands-on experience with game development and C# scripting. Explore level design, grid systems, environmental effects, and systemic gameplay. Understand and implement AI-driven behaviours. Learn how different game systems interact dynamically at runtime. Integrate art, particle effects, and visual elements into your game. Create, polish, and present your own playable game prototype. What You Will Learn Day 1 – Unity & Game Development Fundamentals Unity Fundamentals & Setup Understand what a game engine is and how it powers game development. Get introduced to Unity and its core features. Install Unity and create your first project. Navigate and understand the Unity interface and workspace. Learn to create and use reusable Unity Prefabs. Game Development Fundamentals Build basic levels using simple shapes and prototype gameplay. Learn the fundamentals of C# scripting for game development. Create grid-based systems for structured level design. Implement tile properties and modifiers to influence gameplay. Explore AI fundamentals and basic AI-driven behaviours. Day 2 – Systemic Design & Gameplay Integration Systemic Game Design Understand how interconnected systems shape gameplay. Design systems using variables, rules, and modifiers. Create dynamic environments with interactive elements. Modify system entities and observe their impact on gameplay. Implement AI-driven wildlife and environmental interactions. Gameplay Integration & Polish Connect different game systems to create dynamic interactions. Adjust system values at runtime and simulate changing conditions. Integrate art and visual elements into your prototype. Add particle effects to enhance environmental interactions and gameplay. Polish, finalize, and present a fully playable game. Workshop Format The sessions will combine: Instructor-led concepts Live demonstrations Practical implementation Guided game development System design exercises AI and gameplay experimentation Final game integration and presentation Participants will progressively build their game prototype throughout the workshop.

All that you need to know about Techfest Prompt Engineering Workshop Prompt Engineering Workshop: Prompt Engineering is the practice of turning a raw AI model into a precise, reliable tool  structuring instructions well enough to get accurate, consistent, and usable output every single time. It sits at the intersection of human intent and AI systems, going far beyond "how to talk to ChatGPT" to cover grounding prompts in real data, multimodal inputs, and prompt security  the exact standards enterprise AI teams work with in 2026. Today, this skill is being demanded across every function, not just tech roles: software, finance, healthcare, marketing, legal, and education are all pairing domain expertise with the ability to drive AI effectively, a combination that pays a premium over either skill alone. From building multi-step reasoning chains to structuring content so AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude actually cite it (Generative Engine Optimization, the AI-era equivalent of SEO), businesses now run on well-engineered prompts, not lucky guesses  and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across two intensive offline days at IIT Bombay, you'll go from foundational prompt structures to a real, evaluated prompt system you'll design, test, and refine yourself  no prior AI or coding background required. Workshop Content Foundations of Prompt Engineering Prompt Structuring & Response Shaping Context, Memory & RAG Domain-Specific & Multimodal Prompting Zero-Shot & Few-Shot Learning Advanced Prompting: Chaining & Reasoning Patterns Adaptive & Self-Optimizing Prompt Systems Prompt Security & Evaluation AI Search & GEO Capstone: Build & Test Systems + Certification

title: IIT Bombay's Techfest Agentic AI Workshop
description: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline…
details_text: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline (Concept Sessions, Live Demos & Hands-On Practice) Limited Seat available: About the Workshop Agentic AI represents the biggest paradigm shift in applied artificial intelligence since basic chatbots. Modern enterprise solutions are rapidly evolving from simple single-turn systems to fully autonomous, tool-using agents capable of planning, deciding, and acting. This intensive 2-day hands-on workshop covers the entire agent lifecycle—from core reasoning loops and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to multi-agent orchestration, safety guardrails, and real-world deployment. Participants will build functional agents from scratch using industry-standard frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Why You Should Attend: Master Next-Gen Tech: Deep-dive into the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—the open standard for connecting models directly to enterprise tools and data. Hands-On Experience: Build, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end agents with real-world execution. Framework Mastery: Gain direct technical exposure to LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and vector database integrations. Production-Grade Design: Learn memory management, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) checkpoints, system safety, and token-cost optimization. Workshop Syllabus & Core Topics: Agentic Foundations & Architectures: Transition from chatbots to autonomous agents, master the Sense-Think-Act-Reflect loop, explore operational autonomy levels, and identify failure mitigation strategies. LLM Integration & Prompting: Optimize context windows, implement function calling with JSON schema structured outputs, design production-grade system prompts, and analyze model speed/cost trade-offs. Reasoning & Planning Patterns: Implement multi-step reasoning patterns including ReAct, Reflexion, and Tree-of-Thought alongside automated task decomposition and Orchestrator-Worker routes. Tool Execution & Safety Checkpoints: Design robust tool schemas for deterministic APIs, handle errors with auto-retries, optimize execution (parallel vs. sequential), and integrate Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) safety checks. Model Context Protocol (MCP): Build, connect, and sandbox custom MCP servers using standard Host/Client/Server architecture, primitives, and transport mechanisms (stdio vs. HTTP/SSE). Memory Management & RAG Pipelines: Architect dynamic short-term context and persistent long-term memory using vector databases, context engineering, dynamic session state, and high-retrieval RAG. Multi-Agent Systems & Frameworks: Construct peer-to-peer and hierarchical agent topologies using state handoffs, while comparing leading frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Capstone Build & Deployment: Hands-on experience building, debugging, benchmarking, and applying guardrails to deploy a production agent as an API, Web App, or Chat Interface.

title: Two-Day Global Conference on Emerging Trends in Artificial Intelligence: Comparative Approaches of Legal Governance
description: About the Conference: Date: 20th & 21st November 2026 Venue: Kalinga University Campus Mode: Hybrid Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): SDGs 4, 9, 16, and 17 About Kalinga University: Established in…
details_text: About the Conference: Date: 20th & 21st November 2026 Venue: Kalinga University Campus Mode: Hybrid Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): SDGs 4, 9, 16, and 17 About Kalinga University: Established in 2013, Kalinga University is one of India's leading private universities, strategically located in the Smart City of New Raipur, Chhattisgarh. The University has consistently secured a position among the Top 101–150 Universities in India in the NIRF Rankings 2025 for the fourth consecutive year and has earned NAAC B+ accreditation, reflecting its commitment to academic excellence and quality education. About the Faculty of Law: The Faculty of Law at Kalinga University, Naya Raipur, is committed to promoting academic excellence and professional development in legal education. With a team of distinguished scholars and experienced faculty members, it provides students with a balanced blend of theoretical knowledge and practical skills required to succeed in the evolving legal profession. The Faculty adopts an innovative and holistic approach to legal education through interactive teaching methodologies and experiential learning opportunities. Its curriculum is designed to address contemporary legal challenges, enabling students to develop the knowledge and competencies needed to navigate the complexities of today's legal landscape. Students benefit from modern classrooms, a well-stocked library, a moot courtroom, and an academically stimulating environment that encourages critical thinking, legal research, ethical practice, and professional integrity. Through its commitment to quality education and continuous learning, the Faculty of Law has established itself as a premier destination for aspiring legal professionals. About the Two-Day Global Conference: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies, reshaping legal systems across the world. From automated decision-making in commercial transactions and predictive policing to AI-generated intellectual property and algorithmic tools in judicial processes, AI continues to redefine governance and legal frameworks. While these technologies promise greater efficiency, innovation, and improved access to justice, they also raise significant concerns relating to accountability, transparency, bias, privacy, liability, and the protection of fundamental human rights. As AI technologies continue to evolve, legal systems across different jurisdictions are adopting diverse regulatory approaches. Questions surrounding the authorship of AI-generated works, criminal liability for autonomous systems, algorithmic discrimination in courts, data protection in healthcare technologies, cross-border cyber risks, and international norms governing autonomous weapons have intensified the need for comparative legal dialogue. The absence of uniform global standards further complicates enforcement, jurisdictional accountability, and regulatory harmonisation. Understanding these multidimensional challenges is essential for developing coherent and future-ready legal frameworks. Comparative legal analysis enables policymakers, researchers, and legal scholars to identify best practices, bridge regulatory gaps, and formulate adaptive legal responses. Commercial law, criminal justice, intellectual property, judicial institutions, healthcare regulation, cyber law, and international legal mechanisms must evolve in a balanced manner that promotes innovation while safeguarding constitutional values and human dignity. The Two-Day Global Conference on Emerging Trends in Artificial Intelligence: Comparative Approaches of Legal Governance aims to provide a global platform for dialogue, collaboration, and knowledge exchange among academicians, judges, legal practitioners, policymakers, industry leaders, technologists, and civil society representatives. The conference will feature keynote addresses, panel discussions, research paper presentations, and case study analyses e

title: National Aeromodeling Challenge
description: About: The National Aeromodelling Challenge is presented by Techfest, IIT Bombay, for students passionate about aerospace and engineering. Teams design, build, and fly their own fixed-wing electric RC aircraft that…
details_text: About: The National Aeromodelling Challenge is presented by Techfest, IIT Bombay, for students passionate about aerospace and engineering. Teams design, build, and fly their own fixed-wing electric RC aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads. They first prove their aircraft can carry and land a payload safely, then complete a timed two-trip delivery mission. Ready-made models are not allowed. Bring your aircraft to life at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia’s largest science and technology festival. Structure: The competition has an abstract screening stage, followed by a Qualifier Round and a Main Round at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Eligibility: Open to school, UG, and PG students. Teams can include students from different colleges or schools. Participants must carry a bona fide certificate signed by their HoD/Dean/Principal and a valid ID card. Team Size: 2 to 4 members. A participant can be part of only one team. Problem Statement: Design, build, and fly a fixed-wing aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads (45 g, 43 mm diameter, supplied by organizers) and completes the tasks in each round. Abstract Submission (Online): Submit an abstract of under 15 pages (A4, 1.5 line spacing) in the official Aeromodelling 2026 Abstract Form format. The abstract should cover the aircraft’s basic design (dimensions, wing area, velocity, etc.) and how it suits the problem. Attach a zip file of 5-10 photographs taken while building the aircraft. Abstracts not following the format will not be evaluated. Round 1 - Qualifier Round: Carry one or more golf balls inside the aircraft, fly for at least 30 seconds within a 3-minute window, and land with the payload inside the designated area. Score = (payload weight x 100) / aircraft weight without payload. Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts. The top 30 teams advance to the Main Round. Round 2 - Main Round: Complete a round trip of payload delivery within 3 minutes: load, take off, fly at least 30 seconds, land, unload, reload, take off again, fly at least 30 seconds, land, and unload. Loading must be hands-free, using transmitter-operated compartment doors. Score = E1 + E2 - C1 - C2 - C3. Each delivered golf ball earns 10 points per trip, and each second spent on the ground during loading and unloading costs 1 point. Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts. Overall Score = 0.25 x Normalized Qualifier Score + 0.75 x Normalized Main Round Score. Ties are broken by a separate round framed by the judges. Design Constraints: The aircraft must be designed and built by the team (no RTF/ARF/BNF models). Maximum weight is 1 kg without payload. Thrust-to-weight ratio must not exceed 1 without payload. Wingspan is up to 1.2 m, with no tolerance. Propeller diameter is up to 13 inches, and metal propellers are not allowed. Electric motors only. Gyroscopes, programmed mission steps, FPV, and any flying support are prohibited. Timeline: Registration Deadline: 25th November 2026 Abstract Submission Deadline: 25th November 2026 Abstract Result Announcement: 1st December 2026 Qualifier Round: 15th-16th December 2026 Main Round: 17th December 2026 Rules: Register online to receive a Team ID. No late entries are accepted. The same aircraft described in the abstract must be used in both rounds. Damaged aircraft can be repaired but not replaced. No modifications to the aircraft are allowed after the thrust-to-weight ratio is measured. A 2.4 GHz radio is required. Any other frequency must be informed to the organizers in advance. Landing must be within the inner boundary, otherwise a 20% penalty applies. Touching or crossing the outer boundary disqualifies the attempt. Teams must be ready at their turn, or they lose it. Teams must not share aircraft components with other teams. Safety violations or misconduct will lead to penalties or disqualification. The judges’ and organizers’ decisions are final and binding. Updates will be posted on the Techfest website and sent to registered teams. For official announceme

details_text: Bug Squash is a fast-paced debugging competition where participants must identify and fix bugs in given code snippets within a tight time frame. The challenge spans three increasingly difficult rounds — testing syntax knowledge, logical reasoning, code efficiency, and time management. Teams of two will compete to squash the most bugs in the shortest time. Strategy, focus, and precision will be key to conquering the final round and claiming victory! Prize Pool: Rs. 3500 (Winner : Rs. 2500 + Runner-Up : Rs. 1000) Registration Fee: Rs. 100 Date: 10/12/2026 Event Specific Rules: All teams must participate in all three rounds (if qualified) to be eligible for the final prize. Each team must have exactly 2 members. No substitutions or additions are allowed once Round 2 begins. Each round will have a strict time limit; late submissions will be disqualified for that round. The use of unauthorized tools or devices (e.g., mobile phones, online code editors, AI assistance tools) is strictly prohibited. Code submissions will be monitored by volunteers; plagiarism or copying will lead to immediate disqualification. Organizers reserve the right to verify code originality at any time. In the final round, order of completion will affect scoring — finishing first secures the highest score. The tiebreaker round will be triggered only if there’s an exact tie after Round 3 (including bonus and carried points). Event Structure: Round 1: Syntax Debug Sprint 20-minute individual/team debugging round 50 questions worth 10 points each Bonus points for early completion Top 50% of teams qualify for Round 2 Round 2: Logic Repair Lab 20-minute round with logical error-based problems 10 questions worth 100 points each Bonus for early submission Top 50% of remaining teams (max 8 teams) proceed to Round 3 Round 3: Mixed Bug Battle + Tiebreaker Final round with 2 complex problems per team (syntax + logic) Time limit: 20 minutes Points awarded by order of completion (200 to 120) Additional 10% of Round 2 score added to final tally Tiebreaker Round (if needed): 1 surprise question 10 minutes Worth 20 bonus points Rules: Participants must carry their college ID cards. details_text: Code Battle is a thrilling competitive coding event where logic, speed, and strategy take center stage. Participants face thought-provoking challenges designed to test their skills under pressure, with unexpected twists that keep the competition fierce and unpredictable. More than just a contest, it’s an electrifying experience that celebrates problem-solving, teamwork, and the spirit of coding. After 3 skips, they must solve one question before skipping again. Choosing Questions: Teams may start with any difficulty level. Once a harder box is chosen, teams cannot return to an easier one. A maximum of 5 questions can be solved from each difficulty box. Teams may exchange one question for another of the same difficulty but cannot attempt skipped questions again. Time Limit and Scoring: Total duration: 100 minutes. Allowed languages: C, C++, Java, Python. The winner is decided based on the highest score. In case of a tie, the team with harder problems solved or faster completion time will be declared the winner. Gameplay Procedure: Teams will be seated and given access to the problem sets via HackerRank . Solve problems strategically to maximize score within the given 100 minutes. Keep track of skips, exchanges, and progression to harder levels. Final scores will be tallied, and winners will be announced at the end. General Rules: Carry your college ID card for participation. Arrive at the venue at least 15 minutes before the event starts. Late entries or walk-ins will not be entertained (registration will be canceled). Registration fees are non-refundable. details_text: About DOOMFORGE DOOMFORGE is a two-round business and engineering hackathon that challenges participants to combine strategic thinking, market analysis, and practical software engineering. The competition is designed to take participants beyond conventional coding challenges. It begins with identifying real-world business problems and market opportunities, followed by hands-on engineering challenges involving existing codebases and open-source development. Participants will have the opportunity to demonstrate their analytical thinking, technical expertise, creativity, and ability to build practical solutions. Eligibility and Team Formation Open to college students. Team size: 1 - 3 members. Inter-college teams are allowed. Participants from different academic specialisations are welcome to collaborate. Each participant can be part of only one team. All team members must complete the registration process. Competition Structure Round 1: Market Analysis Duration: 4 December – 6 December 2026 Round 1 focuses on business strategy, market research, and problem identification. Participants will be presented with a business-oriented problem or scenario. They must analyse the problem, understand the market landscape, identify opportunities, and propose a feasible solution. What participants need to cover: Problem identification and understanding. Target audience and market analysis. Competitor research and existing solutions. Identification of market gaps and opportunities. Proposed solution, its feasibility, and potential impact. Submission Format: Teams must submit a one-minute video explaining their market analysis, identified opportunity, and proposed solution through Unstop. Evaluation Criteria: Depth of market research. Understanding of the problem. Originality and innovation. Feasibility of the proposed solution. Clarity and effectiveness of presentation. Based on their submissions, selected teams will qualify for the second round. Round 2: Engineering Arena – Open-Source Development The second round is a hands-on engineering challenge in which shortlisted teams will work on one of four dedicated GitHub repositories. Each repository represents a distinct engineering track with its own technical problem space. Participants will be expected to understand the existing codebase, identify areas for improvement, and implement meaningful technical contributions. Potential engineering challenges include: Developing new features and functionalities. Identifying and fixing bugs. Improving application performance and scalability. Implementing security enhancements. Writing automated tests and improving test coverage. Integrating AI/ML-based capabilities. Improving code quality, maintainability, and documentation. Submission Format: All development contributions must be submitted through GitHub Pull Requests (PRs) to the respective repositories. Evaluation Criteria: Functional correctness and completeness. Code quality and maintainability. Technical implementation. Security and reliability. Testing and validation. Innovation and practical impact. Engineering Tracks DOOMFORGE features four specialised engineering tracks, each backed by a dedicated GitHub repository. Participants will work on the repository and technical challenge specified by the organising team. Further details regarding the repositories, technical requirements, and challenges will be communicated to qualified participants. Rules and Regulations Teams must consist of a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3 members. Inter-college participation is permitted. Each participant may register as part of only one team. Round 1 submissions must be submitted within the specified deadline, from 4 December to 6 December 2026. Round 1 submissions must follow the prescribed one-minute video format. details_text: About: An engaging mix of algorithmic strategy, autonomous decision-making, and competitive resource management, this event puts participants in command of programmable rover fleets competing for dominance on an unpredictable battlefield. Participants must design intelligent controllers to explore unfamiliar terrain, gather resources, defend their territory, and outmanoeuvre rival teams. With mechanics ranging from hidden hazards and tactical combat to resource-driven upgrades and enemy vault raids, every decision can shift the balance of the game. The event tests participants' programming skills, strategic thinking, adaptability, and ability to make optimal decisions under uncertainty. The event will unfold in two stages . Prelims (Online): Format: Submission-based programming round hosted on Unstop. Description: Participants develop and submit autonomous rover controllers to compete in a head-to-head, turn-based strategy game. The round challenges participants to explore a simulated environment, gather resources, and outmanoeuvre their opponents through intelligent decision-making. Algorithmic thinking, tactical planning, and efficient resource management are key to advancing. Finals (Offline): Format: On-site interactive competition conducted at IIT Madras. Description: Shortlisted participants compete in a live, turn-based rover strategy game featuring a free-for-all format. Participants must program their rovers to explore the map, mine resources, raid enemy vaults, engage in combat, and manage upgrades to maximise their score. The finals also introduce a dynamic in-game market, adding an economic dimension where participants must make strategic decisions about resource allocation, purchases, and upgrades. Adaptability, tactical thinking, and intelligent resource management will be crucial to securing victory. Date: To be held during Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras. The event follows a team-based format, with 2–3 participants per team, encouraging collaboration in algorithm design, strategic planning, and resource management. Participants must combine their analytical abilities and technical skills to develop competitive rover controllers and devise effective strategies.

title: Boeing Aeromodelling Competition
description: Event Description Abstract Submission Round Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs.…
details_text: Event Description Abstract Submission Round Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs. The abstract should cover the aircraft design, including dimensions, wing area, estimated flight speed, reservoir and mounting, release mechanism, leakage prevention, centre-of-gravity management, and safe operation. The prescribed format must be downloaded from the respective IIT website and submitted by email at least 20 days before the competition. Shortlisted teams will be announced 15 days before the competition. If multiple teams participate from the same institution, their aircraft designs must be distinct, with at least a 2.5% difference in wingspan, chord, and fuselage length; otherwise, the teams will be disqualified. Qualifier Round The Qualifier Round aims to select the top 30 teams with lightweight aircraft capable of safe, controlled flight carrying a 1,000 mL water payload. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds with the full payload, with no water release required. The water must be stored in a sealed, securely mounted, removable reservoir, with the reservoir and release mechanism included in the aircraft’s empty weight. Judges will inspect the system before takeoff, and there must be no visible leakage. Each attempt must be completed within 3 minutes. Failure to maintain 30 seconds of safe flight or any visible leakage before landing results in a zero score. Each team gets two attempts, with the higher score counted, and only teams that safely complete the loaded flight can advance. The top 30 teams qualify for the Main Round and receive ₹5,000 towards material costs, subject to providing the bank details of one designated team member. Main Round In the Main Round, the aircraft must carry 1,000 mL of water in an inspected, sealed, removable reservoir and release it while flying over the designated simulated fire/release zone. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds before release, which must be manually triggered by the pilot using a single transmitter channel; automatic or programmed release is not allowed. Judges will verify that the release begins within the marked zone, which is approximately 40 m from the take-off/landing area, though its location and dimensions may be adjusted based on venue and wind conditions. The amount of water released will be determined by weighing the reservoir before and after the attempt; if leakage before the commanded release cannot be distinguished from the actual release, the attempt scores zero. Each team gets two attempts, with the better score counted, and each attempt must complete the release and landing within 3 minutes. Rules and Regulations The same aircraft must be used throughout all rounds and must match the submitted design; repairs are allowed, but replacement aircraft are not. Teams should carry spare components and be ready when called, or risk losing their attempt or flight time. A 2.4 GHz radio is required unless another frequency is approved in advance, receivers must remain in receiver mode only, and metal propellers are prohibited. All systems will be inspected before the competition, and non-functional equipment can lead to dismissal. Teams must carry their own equipment and cannot share components with other teams. Aircraft may use powered take-off with landing gear or manual launch. A team member cannot participate in more than one team. Teams must be ready to fly after the 120-second interval following the previous attempt or lose their turn. Reimbursement will only be made to a registered team member whose bank account name matches the registration details. Flying outside the designated zone will result in disqualification, and the aircraft must immediately return and land safely. The take-off, landing, and release zones may vary depending on venue and wind conditions. Teams may participate in only one zonal ev

title: Pixels To Prognosis
description: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different…
details_text: About the Event Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different radiologists often draw the boundaries differently. Pixels to Prognosis asks you to build an AI system that does this automatically. Using multimodal brain MRI scans, your model has to locate a glioma and separate it into its three subregions: active (enhancing) tumour, necrotic core, and surrounding edema. The event combines neuroscience, MRI physics and computer vision. You’ll need more than a model with a good leaderboard score. You’ll also need to understand what the scans show, why models fail, and how to make one that holds up on real clinical data. Who Can Participate Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college and any stream Especially suited to students in Biotechnology & Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and AI & Data Science Teams of 1 to 3 members . Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Quiz (Screening) This is a case-based quiz on: How MRI machines work and the basics of MRI imaging The biology of brain gliomas and how they appear on MRI scans Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Image Processing The questions reward reasoning over memorisation. The quiz is meant to sharpen your problem-solving for the later rounds. Round 2: Model Submission Round Shortlisted teams train a segmentation model on a curated glioma dataset we provide, [derived from the BraTS 2021 challenge]. Each patient has four MRI modalities: T1-weighted, post-contrast T1-weighted (T1ce), T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR. Your model must segment three regions: Whole Tumour, Tumour Core and Enhancing Tumour. Models are ranked on a hidden patient-level test set . Rules: Train only on the dataset provided. No external data. All learnable parameters must start from random initialisation . Pretrained weights are not allowed. You may use published architectures such as U-Net variants. The Colab notebook runtime must be 9 hours or less . Submission requirements: Complete source code (.py / .ipynb) Final trained weights (.pt / .keras) Training logs, including loss and validation curves, config and seed used (.csv) A technical report (.pdf) covering your thought process, pipeline, architecture details and the compute you used Evaluation: Segmentation quality is measured with the Dice score and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance for each tumour region. Scoring also covers anatomical consistency, false-positive control, and the quality of your technical report. Finals: Offline Round at IIT Madras Finalists come to campus and receive a new set of MRI scans with real-world problems. These can include motion artefacts, missing modalities, or pathologies your model has never seen. Each team must: Work out what is wrong with the data and why it happened Adapt the model through preprocessing, retraining or other corrective strategies Present the problems they found, the medical reasoning behind them, and how they handled them Evaluation criteria: Problem identification and medical reasoning Model adaptation strategy and outcome Clarity of presentation and understanding Knowing when your model should not be trusted counts in your favour. Flagging an unreliable case for expert review is part of good clinical AI. Prizes & Recognition Cash prizes for the top 3 teams [prize pool: ₹35000] Special Awards for Best Robust Model and Best Diagnostic Reasoning Certificates of Merit for the winners(Hard Copy) Certificates of Merit for all finalists(Soft Copy) Certificates of Participation for all Round 2 participants Important Dates Registration closes: 28th December, 2026 Round 1 (Online Quiz): 5th December, 2026 Round 2 submission window: 9th - 16th December, 2026 Finals at IIT Madras: 4th January, 2027

Each challenge will test different aspects of cybersecurity knowledge and technical expertise. The event is meant to promote cybersecurity awareness, encourage ethical hacking practices, and create a platform for collaboration among students passionate about security. This event will be conducted offline at IIIT Bhubaneswar, giving participants a chance to interact with cybersecurity enthusiasts, mentors, and experts from different colleges.

details_text: About the Event: Slay CTF is a thrilling, jeopardy-style Capture The Flag competition designed to test your offensive security skills, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Whether you are a beginner looking to break into the world of cybersecurity or a seasoned hacker hunting for complex challenges, Slay CTF offers a dynamic environment to exploit vulnerabilities, crack ciphers, and trace digital footprints. Put your skills to the test, climb the global leaderboard, and prove your mettle in the ultimate battle of bits and bytes! Eligibility & Registration Guidelines: Target Audience: Open to all students (UG/PG/Diploma), early-career professionals, and self-taught security enthusiasts. Inter-College Teams: Allowed and highly encouraged. Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed (Open to all branches and backgrounds). Team Size: Participate individually or in teams of [1 - 3 members] . Prerequisites: Eagerness to learn. Challenge Categories (Topics) The CTF will feature a diverse set of challenges scaled from beginner to advanced difficulties across the following domains: Web Exploitation: Uncover vulnerabilities in web applications (e.g., SQLi, XSS, IDOR, SSRF). OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Track down hidden information and piece together digital trails across the public internet. Cryptography: Break encryption schemes, decode ciphers, and analyze cryptographic protocols. Digital Forensics: Analyze memory dumps, network packet captures (PCAPs), and hidden file metadata. Reverse Engineering: Deconstruct compiled binaries and understand their underlying logic. Miscellaneous / Sanity: Brain-teasers, scripting challenges, and out-of-the-box puzzles. Event Format & Process Format: Hybrid (Online + JGEC Campus), Jeopardy-Style CTF. Platform: Challenges will be hosted on our dedicated infrastructure ( CTFd). Duration: The competition will run continuously for 3 hours . Scoring System: Dynamic scoring will be implemented (the point value of a challenge decreases as more teams solve it). Process: Once registered on Unstop, team leaders will receive the platform link and credentials via email 24 hours prior to the event kickoff. Rules & Code of Conduct No Flag Sharing: Sharing flags or solutions with other teams is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification of all involved parties. No Brute-Forcing: Automated brute-forcing of the flag submission platform or challenge infrastructure is forbidden unless explicitly mentioned in the challenge description. No Attacking the Infrastructure: Do not launch Denial of Service (DoS/DDoS) attacks or attempt to compromise the hosting servers. Collaboration: You are free to use Google, AI tools, and public documentation, but collaboration is strictly limited to your own team members. Final Decisions: The organizing team's decisions regarding scoring, disputes, and disqualifications are final and binding. Prizes & Perks Cash Prize, Certification Vouchers and goodies. [NOTE: Cash Prizes and Goodies exclusively for offline participation] Official Certificate of Participation for those who solve at least one challenge.

title: AETHOS - Day Zero
description: If civilization had to begin again tomorrow, what would humanity build first? Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the…
details_text: If civilization had to begin again tomorrow, what would humanity build first? Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the foundations of an entirely new civilization. Participants are encouraged to think beyond applications and incremental improvements. Every project should solve a meaningful challenge that contributes to rebuilding society—whether through communication, energy, healthcare, infrastructure, education, resilience, exploration, or entirely new approaches that redefine the future. This is not about recreating yesterday. It is about engineering tomorrow. The Mission: Design and develop an innovative solution that would help humanity rebuild after the collapse of modern civilization. Your project may be software, hardware, embedded systems, IoT, AI, robotics, communication systems, cybersecurity, biotechnology, space technology, sustainable engineering, or any interdisciplinary solution aligned with the mission. Projects should focus on solving real-world problems with practical engineering, long-term scalability, and meaningful societal impact. Civilization Pillars: Every project belongs to one of the official Civilization Pillars that represent the essential functions required to rebuild society. The detailed descriptions of all pillars are provided separately. Choose the pillar that best represents the purpose of your solution, not simply the technologies you use. Who Can Participate? Students from any recognized institution are welcome. Participants from all engineering, science, technology, design, management, and interdisciplinary backgrounds are encouraged. Teams must follow the team size specified on the registration page. Innovation thrives when diverse disciplines work together. What Can You Build? We welcome projects across a wide range of domains, including but not limited to: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Embedded Systems & Electronics Internet of Things (IoT) Robotics & Automation Wireless Communication Systems Healthcare & Medical Technologies Renewable Energy Smart Infrastructure Disaster Management Cybersecurity Space & Aerospace Technologies Sustainability Human-Centered Design Frontier & Moonshot Innovations If your solution contributes meaningfully to rebuilding civilization, it belongs here. Submission Requirements: Teams should be prepared to submit: Project presentation Technical documentation Source code repository Prototype or proof of concept Demonstration video (if applicable) Additional submission guidelines and templates will be shared with registered participants. Evaluation: Projects will be assessed on their overall contribution toward rebuilding civilization, including: Innovation Engineering excellence Technical feasibility Scalability Societal impact Resilience Quality of presentation The complete judging rubric is available in the attached documentation. General Rules: All submitted work must be original. Open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools may be used with proper attribution. AI-assisted development is permitted unless otherwise specified. Plagiarism or intellectual property violations will result in immediate disqualification. Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and uphold the event's code of conduct. Decisions made by the organizing committee and judging panel will be final. A comprehensive rulebook is available in the attached resources. Why Participate? DAY ZERO is more than a competition. It is an opportunity to think like the engineers who would shape the first generation of a new civilization. Challenge assumptions. Collaborate across disciplines. Build technologies that matter. Engineer systems that could redefine humanity's future. Tomorrow Begins Here. History remembers the civilizations that were built. The next one starts with your idea.

details_text: Business Analytics Workshop: Business Analytics is the practice of turning raw business data into clear, actionable decisions. It sits at the intersection of business thinking and data tools - using spreadsheets, databases, and visualization platforms to spot patterns, forecast trends, and answer real business questions. Today, this practice is being reshaped by AI: natural-language queries, auto-generated insights, and AI-assisted dashboards are changing how analysts work, making the skill faster to learn and more powerful to apply. From sales and marketing to operations and finance, businesses now run on dashboards, not gut feeling - and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across one intensive day, you'll go from raw, messy data to a real dashboard and a business recommendation you'll actually present - no prior coding or analytics background required. details_text: ANAVARAN, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is an immersive sustainability investigation and strategy competition that challenges participants to uncover the gap between corporate sustainability claims and ground realities. Teams of four step into the roles of Sustainability Investigators and Corporate Strategists, investigating Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd., a fictional organisation whose green image may not reflect its actual environmental and social impact. Across three challenging rounds, participants will identify greenwashing, investigate hidden contradictions, assess business risks and develop commercially viable sustainability strategies under real-world-inspired crises. From questioning environmental claims to defending strategic decisions before a jury, ANAVARAN tests critical thinking, ESG awareness, analytical ability and the power to build a genuinely sustainable future. ROUND 1 – GREEN OR GREENWASH? Spot the Illusion Teams will receive a collection of fictional ESG claims, advertisements, sustainability statements, corporate announcements and certification claims made by Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. regarding its proposed Hooghly Data Park in West Bengal. Participants must critically examine each of the 10 claims and classify them into one of three categories: Genuine Sustainability Greenwashing Misleading Communication Each classification must be supported by a short justification explaining what is being promised, whether the claim is verifiable, what important information is missing and whether the communication creates an exaggerated positive impression. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop. Format: ESG Claim Classification + Justification Brief. Case: Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. – Hooghly Data Park. Number of Claims: 10. Submission: Each claim must include its classification and a justification of 3–6 lines. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation Criteria: Classification Accuracy – 50% Quality of Justification – 40% Clarity of Expression – 10% ROUND 2 – THE GREENWASH FILES Uncover the Truth The qualifying teams will receive a comprehensive investigation dossier containing public statements, internal technical documents, employment projections, renewable energy plans, community partnership updates and environmental assessments relating to Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. Teams must investigate the contradictions between the company's public sustainability commitments and its internal operational realities. Participants must identify instances of greenwashing, uncover misleading disclosures, assess environmental and social implications, and evaluate the financial, regulatory and reputational risks arising from these gaps. Teams will present their investigation findings and risk assessment before the jury. Round Details: Mode: Offline. Timing: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (as specified in the event brochure). Format: Case Investigation + Jury Findings Presentation. Case: Detailed investigation of Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd.'s Hooghly Data Park. Qualification: Top 6 Teams advance to Round 3 (Grand Finale). Key Areas of Investigation: Water consumption, groundwater stress and water-positive claims. Renewable energy commitments and net-zero targets. Employment claims and actual local job creation. Farmer partnerships and treated wastewater utilisation. Green certifications and environmental compliance. Financial, regulatory, reputational and social risks. In this three-round competition, teams of four take charge of a virtual war chest and compete to build the strongest business portfolio through strategic bidding, market decisions and resource allocation. From acquiring valuable assets and managing capital to navigating market shocks and defending their final strategy, participants must demonstrate financial judgment, risk management, adaptability and strategic thinking. Victory belongs not to the highest spender, but to the team that makes the smartest decisions. Assemble your team, bid strategically and build your empire! ROUND 1 – THE GRAND AUCTION Bid to Build Every registered team begins with an equal virtual capital allocation and enters a live, open-floor auction featuring a fixed catalogue of business assets, including brands, companies, technology, talent and market opportunities. details_text: Step into the world of Human Resource Management with SAMAYKRAM, the HR flagship competition at XAVIESTA 5.0, presented under the theme KAALCHAKRA. Inspired by the idea that every people decision shapes an organisation's future, this three-round challenge takes participants through workforce diagnosis, live HR dilemmas and future workforce strategy. From uncovering hidden organisational challenges through employee data to managing critical workplace decisions and navigating workforce disruptions, teams must demonstrate analytical thinking, strategic HR knowledge, leadership and adaptability. Assemble your team of four and experience the challenges of managing people, making decisions and shaping the future of work. Teams will receive a confidential dossier containing employee records, engagement survey results, attrition patterns and workplace incident logs related to Kaalmanav Group. Participants must independently investigate the provided information, identify the organisation's core HR challenge, uncover its root cause and submit a written diagnosis supported by evidence. details_text: KaalDrishti, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is a business analytics competition that challenges participants to step into the role of Data Investigators and uncover the truth behind a company's crisis. Teams of four will work with fragmented financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business information to identify hidden patterns, detect anomalies and establish the real cause of a problem. Across three challenging rounds, participants will investigate an unsolved business crisis, tackle analytical challenges and defend their conclusions through hypothesis testing and a live boardroom presentation. The event tests analytical thinking, data interpretation, statistical reasoning, problem-solving and the ability to convert data into meaningful business decisions. ROUND 1 – THE CRIME SCENE: FIND THE STORY Project Mirage – Uncover the Hidden Truth Participants will receive a business scenario, problem statement and relevant datasets. The case file will contain fragmented information such as financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business evidence. Teams must independently understand the situation, identify relevant patterns and anomalies, determine the root cause of the crisis and develop a hypothesis explaining what went wrong and why. Based on their analysis, teams must propose feasible business solutions while complying with the given constraints. Round Details: Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Open-Ended Data Investigation + Written Hypothesis Brief Submission: PDF deck of maximum 10 pages, excluding the Introduction and Closing slides. Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation Criteria: Understanding of the problem and root cause analysis. Analytical rigour specific to the dataset. Methodology adopted. Feasibility and quality of the proposed business solution. ROUND 2 – THE LOCKED DATA: UNLOCK THE EVIDENCE Xcelerate – Excel E-Sports The qualifying teams will enter an analytical challenge where they will be provided with a dataset and a problem statement. Participants must analyse the given information and develop an optimised solution or analytical model according to the requirements. Teams will be required to demonstrate their analytical capabilities using Microsoft Excel. They can use Excel charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins to develop and present their solutions. However, the final solution must be presented entirely in Excel. The methodology adopted and the plugins used must be explicitly mentioned. Round Details: Mode: Offline Format: Dataset-Based Analytical Modelling and Excel Challenge. Tools: Microsoft Excel, Excel Charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins. Submission/Presentation: The solution must be presented in Excel only. Qualification: Top 5 Teams advance to Round 3. Evaluation Focus: Analytical reasoning. Data interpretation and modelling. Problem-solving ability. Efficiency and accuracy of the solution. Methodology and effective use of Excel tools. ROUND 3 – THE FALSE TRAIL & THE BOARDROOM TRIAL: DELIVER THE VERDICT Find the Real Cause. Defend It Under Fire. The finalists will be presented with multiple plausible explanations for the company's crisis, each supported by a different set of evidence. Only one explanation will represent the actual cause. Teams must test each hypothesis against the evidence collected in the earlier rounds, identify explanations based on bias, false correlation or manipulated data, and trace the crisis back to its Point of No Return — the exact past decision that set the crisis in motion. Participants will then present their final verdict and business recommendations before a jury acting as the company's Board, which will cross-examine their assumptions and conclusions. Round Details: Mode: Offline – Live Defence, Grand Finale. Format: Hypothesis Testing + Live Verdict Presentation + Jury Cross-Examination. details_text: Overview YUGANTAR, presented by FINNOVATION as part of XAVIESTA 5.0, is an immersive marketing strategy competition that challenges participants to rewrite the destiny of a fictional Indian footwear brand. Through three interconnected rounds, teams will investigate the brand's history, uncover the strategic decision behind its downfall, rewrite a defining moment in its journey, and navigate the consequences of their choices. From analysing fragmented evidence and developing revised marketing strategies to tackling real-time marketing crises, participants must demonstrate their consumer understanding, analytical thinking, creativity and strategic decision-making. Here, every decision shapes the future, and every consequence tells a story. Round 1 – The Archive Decode the Brand Teams will receive a fragmented case archive containing old advertisements, consumer reviews, sales data, competitor movements, internal memos and market research relating to Kadam Footwear, a fictional Indian footwear brand. Participants must reconstruct the brand's timeline, identify the single strategic decision that changed its destiny and support their conclusions with evidence from the provided documents. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Fragmented Evidence Reconstruction + Written Hypothesis Brief Submission: One PDF containing: Reconstructed timeline of 8–12 events in chronological order. Hypothesis brief of maximum 500 words. Supporting evidence with document references. Qualification: Top 12 Teams Evaluation: Timeline accuracy, identification of the turning-point decision, evidence-based analysis and critical thinking. Round 2 – The Butterfly Effect Rewrite the Past The qualifying teams will get an opportunity to change one defining decision from Kadam Footwear's history. They must analyse how this single intervention could have altered the brand's journey, considering its impact on brand equity, market share, profit margins, competitive positioning and consumer perception. Based on their revised historical scenario, teams must develop a coherent marketing strategy and justify the consequences of their chosen intervention. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline Format: Single-Decision Rewrite + Revised Strategy Brief Challenge: Rewriting one historical decision and analysing its consequences. Submission: Revised strategy brief. Qualification: Top 6 Teams Evaluation: Strategic coherence, consequence analysis, marketing strategy, positioning and decision-making. Round 3 – The Present Break & Break the Chakra Survive 2027, Then Choose the Future The final round brings the consequences of each team's revised decision into the present. Each finalist will face a team-specific marketing crisis shaped by the changes introduced in Round 2. Teams must allocate a limited marketing budget across digital marketing, influencers, product, retail, partnerships and consumer research to respond to the crisis. They will then face a CEO-level dilemma, choosing whether to Accept, Alter or Reset the brand's future direction. The challenge concludes with a live boardroom presentation and jury cross-examination, where teams must defend their strategy and decisions. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline – Live Defence Format: Crisis Budget Allocation + CEO Dilemma + Jury Presentation & Cross-Examination Challenge: Team-specific marketing crisis and strategic decision-making. Finalists: Top 6 Teams from Round 2 Evaluation: Crisis management, resource allocation, consumer understanding, creativity, brand vision and strategic defence. description: Date: 21st November Registration fees: 200 per participant Overview PERPLEXED is built around two partner companies whose businesses depend on each other, and both are struggling. Half the teams act as consulting firms…
details_text: Date: 21st November Registration fees: 200 per participant Overview PERPLEXED is built around two partner companies whose businesses depend on each other, and both are struggling. Half the teams act as consulting firms hired by Company A, and the other half are hired by Company B. The problems are real within the game, but are not given to teams directly. Teams discover them by interviewing AI chatbots playing company stakeholders, such as the CEO, CFO, operations head, HR manager or disgruntled employee. Each stakeholder knows only part of the story and may have their own agenda, hide or downplay facts, or misremember events. Teams must ask effective questions, connect clues, distinguish facts from spin, and present a clear diagnosis with practical recommendations to judges acting as the client's board. Not everything worth knowing is said out loud: the company portal also holds traces of everyday office life that may quietly support or contradict what stakeholders claim. Neither company's problems can be solved from inside one company: part of every root cause sits with the partner, and employees on each side may be quick to blame the other. Midway through the investigation, each team must find and convince a team working on the other company to form an alliance, combine what both sides know, and present a joint diagnosis. Eligibility: Open to students. Teams of 2-4. Performance Guidelines: Robots or simulated bots must follow arena rules and size limits. Online teams use the provided simulator; on-site teams must pass inspection. Robots may be modified between rounds. Judging Criteria Match results (50%) Strategy (20%) Robot performance (20%) Adaptation between rounds (10%).
