details_text: Date of Event: 20th November 2026 Registration Fee: 300 per Participant Overview The Venture Ecosystem is an eight-hour overnight simulation in which three tracks, Product, Consulting, and Finance, operate in parallel while influencing one another. Product teams create and develop startups; Consulting teams solve business cases, advise startups, and tackle shared crises; Finance teams evaluate investments, manage portfolios, and trade owned equity only with other Finance teams. Over the night, teams move through a foundation round, a first Deal Room, a shared crisis with a controlled secondary-market window, and a final Ultimate Venture Challenge in which all three tracks collaborate on one last resource-allocation plan. The guiding idea: Product creates value, Consulting unlocks value, and Finance allocates value. Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate and postgraduate students from any recognized institution. Teams of 2-4. Cross-college teams are allowed. Only qualifier-selected teams can attend the on-site round. Performance Guidelines: Designs must be created within the time window; use of AI-generated ready designs must be declared. Submit a Figma link or file and a short rationale. All assets must be original or properly licensed. Judging Criteria Usability (30%) Visual design (25%) Innovation (20%) Problem-solution fit (15%) Presentation of rationale (10%).

title: Building Brands - The Streetwear Business Challenge
description: The Streetwear Business Challenge: What does it really take to build a successful fashion brand? A great design is only the beginning. Behind every successful fashion label lies a strong supply chain, a compelling…
details_text: The Streetwear Business Challenge: What does it really take to build a successful fashion brand? A great design is only the beginning. Behind every successful fashion label lies a strong supply chain, a compelling marketing strategy, and a distribution model that converts creativity into commercial success. The Tough Ones invites aspiring entrepreneurs, marketers, strategists, and business enthusiasts to participate in Building Brands – The Streetwear Business Challenge. This is a real-world case competition where participants will take on the role of business strategists and work on practical challenges faced by an emerging streetwear brand. Across three rounds, participants will: Identify and evaluate potential T-shirt manufacturers and suppliers. Compare actual quotations, pricing, quality, and supplier credibility. Develop a marketing strategy aligned with the brand's identity and target audience. Build a practical distribution and sales strategy to take the products to market. This is your opportunity to move beyond classroom concepts and experience the decisions involved in building and scaling a fashion business. Think Like A Founder. Strategise Like A Consultant. Execute Like A Brand Builder.: Who Can Participate?: Students from all academic backgrounds are welcome, particularly those interested in: Business Management and Entrepreneurship Marketing and Digital Marketing Fashion Management and Fashion Business Commerce and Finance Supply Chain and Operations Sales, Retail and E-commerce No prior experience in the fashion industry is required.

details_text: UDGAM'27 Campus Ambassador Program Welcome to the UDGAM'27 Campus Ambassador Program, where passion meets opportunity! E-Cell, IIT Guwahati, is dedicated to promoting entrepreneurship and nurturing innovation among young minds. Through UDGAM, our annual entrepreneurship summit, we aim to bring together aspiring entrepreneurs, innovators, industry leaders, and students to create meaningful opportunities and experiences. The UDGAM'27 Campus Ambassador Program is an internship initiative designed to develop entrepreneurial mindsets, leadership abilities, and professional skills among students. As a bridge between E-Cell, IIT Guwahati, and your college, you will get the opportunity to explore the startup ecosystem, enhance your communication and marketing skills, build valuable connections, and contribute to one of the region's biggest entrepreneurship summits. Workshops on career development, entrepreneurship, marketing, and other fields. Verifiable certificates upon successful completion. Letter of Recommendation for top-performing Campus Ambassadors. Top performers will get Exclusive goodies such as T-shirts, badges, and more. Top performers will be featured on the social media platforms of E-Cell, IIT Guwahati. Free UDGAM'27 passes for top-performing Campus Ambassadors. Responsibilities Act as the primary point of contact between E-Cell, IIT Guwahati, and your college community. Promote UDGAM'27 and its events, competitions, and initiatives across your respective college. Create awareness through social media platforms, college groups, and other communication channels. Encourage student participation and drive registrations for UDGAM'27 events. Identify and connect with students interested in entrepreneurship, innovation, and startups. details_text: Event Overview: MarkQuizzz invites curious minds, marketing enthusiasts, and business aficionados to participate in an exciting inter-college quiz that tests their knowledge of marketing, brands, advertising, business awareness, and current affairs. Designed to challenge participants knowledge, logical thinking, and teamwork, Markquizzz offers an engaging platform to compete against some of the brightest minds from colleges and institutions. Event Structure Round 1: The Qualifier – Written Marketing Sprint Teams will attempt 20 questions within 20 minutes. Questions will cover marketing fundamentals, brands, advertising, consumer behaviour, business awareness, and current affairs. Questions will be projected or read out, and teams must record their answers on the official answer sheets. Top-scoring teams will qualify for the stage finale. Round 2: The Stage Final – The Battle of Brands Shortlisted teams will compete across four exciting segments: Segment A – Rapid Fire: 60 seconds per team to answer 5 questions. +10 marks for every correct answer; no marks for incorrect answers or passes. Segment B – Visual & Audio: Identify logos, advertisements, taglines, brand sounds, packaging, and personalities. +10 marks for every correct answer. Segment C – Connect the Dots: Identify the common connection among 3–4 clues. +15 marks for every correct answer. Segment D – Buzzer Battle: An open buzzer round testing participants' speed and accuracy. +10 marks for a correct answer and -5 marks for an incorrect answer or over-attempt, as per the quizmaster's rules. Scores will accumulate across all four segments. In case of a tie, a tie-breaker question will determine the final ranking. Rules & Regulations Team Size: Exactly 3 participants per team. A maximum of 14 teams will be accommodated. Multiple teams from the same college/institution are permitted. Only registered team members are allowed to participate. Electronic devices, including mobile phones, smartwatches, and tablets, are strictly prohibited during the active quiz rounds. Any attempt to use unfair means may result in immediate disqualification. The decision of the quizmaster and organising committee will be final and binding. Awards & Recognition Winner: Prize/Gift Hamper worth Rs 3000 + Certificate Runner-up: Prize/Gift Hamper worth Rs 2000 + Certificate Certificates/Mementos for finalists. E-Participation Certificates for participants. Key Highlights An exciting inter-college marketing and business quiz. Four dynamic stage-final segments testing knowledge, speed, and presence of mind. A chance to showcase expertise in marketing, brands, advertising, and business. Competitive exposure and interaction with students from different institutions. Think Fast. Know More. Buzz First! Get ready to put your marketing knowledge to the ultimate test at MAXFEST 5.0! Contact: Arya - 6204601088 Bhaskar - 8800871816

details_text: Think. Predict. Detect. Challenge AI. EvoCopilot Student Chapter at Bharati Vidyapeeth (Deemed to be University), College of Engineering, Pune, presents ESC AI Quest 2026 — an inter-year AI and reasoning quiz competition open to students from First Year, Second Year, Third Year, and Final Year. Challenge yourself through AI concepts, logical reasoning, output prediction, prompt engineering, debugging, and AI-generated content analysis. This is not a conventional coding competition. The quiz is designed to test your thinking, problem-solving, and understanding of AI rather than only advanced programming knowledge. Eligibility: Open to students from all years of undergraduate study. Students from all eligible colleges/organizations can participate, subject to the registration settings. Individual participation. Every participant will receive the same question set. Competition Format: Online quiz hosted on Unstop. Multiple-choice and scenario-based questions. Questions covering AI fundamentals, logic and reasoning, output prediction, prompt engineering, debugging, and AI error detection. A mix of easy, medium, and challenging questions. Participants must complete the quiz within the announced time limit. Rules: Each participant must register individually. Participants must use their own registered account. The same questions and scoring rules will apply to everyone. No collaboration, sharing of answers, or impersonation is allowed. External assistance or AI tools must not be used during the quiz unless explicitly permitted by the organizers. Participants must follow the time limit and instructions provided on Unstop. The organizers' decision regarding scores, tie-breakers, and results will be final. Selection And Results: Participants will be ranked according to their quiz scores. In case of a tie, the organizers may use completion time or a tie-breaker question, depending on the platform's available scoring features. The highest-scoring participant will be declared the ESC AI Quest 2026 Champion. Why Participate?: Test your AI and logical reasoning skills. Challenge participants from different academic years. Explore AI beyond traditional coding. Compete for recognition as the ESC AI Quest Champion. Think you can outsmart the challenge? Register and put your reasoning skills to the test!

details_text: Guidelines: The competition is open for all (School students, undergraduate students, postgraduate students, MBA/PGDM students, etc.). Participants can be from either the same or different academic years. The competition is divided into 3 Rounds. Round 1 will be an Online Quiz. Round 2 will be PPT. Round 3 will be the final Pitch Up round . The panel decision would be final and binding on all the participants. Judging parameters and further details would be communicated to the qualifying teams through email. The decision of Panellist and Team Prarambh will be final and binding to all the participants. Round-1: Quiz on Unstop Only the team leader can attend this section. The section will contain Start-up Related and Decision making questions. There will be 20 questions in this section. The time allotted for the quiz is 2 0 minutes . There will be no negative marking. This is an elimination round, and only the qualifying teams will proceed to Round 2. Elimination will be based on the scores. Round-2: Submission on Unstop Only the Qualified teams from Round 1 will be able to play Round 2. This is an elimination round, and only the qualifying teams will proceed to Round 3. Elimination will be based on the scores (Practicality of the business idea, Market potential and feasibility of execution). Round-3: Pitch Up on Campus Qualified teams from Round 2 will go to the final round i.e., Round 3. They will have to pitch their Business Plan in front of the panellists. Judging parameters and further details will be communicated to the qualifying teams through email. The decision of judges and Team Prarambh will be final and binding to all the participants.

title: CHAKRAVYUH - The Flagship Business Event Of Xaviesta 5.0

description: Step into the world of strategic business leadership with CHAKRAVYUH, the flagship business event of XAVIESTA 5.0, inspired by the theme KAALCHAKRA. Through three interconnected rounds, teams take charge of Trikaal…
details_text: Step into the world of strategic business leadership with CHAKRAVYUH, the flagship business event of XAVIESTA 5.0, inspired by the theme KAALCHAKRA. Through three interconnected rounds, teams take charge of Trikaal Industries, a fictional conglomerate, navigating its past, present and future. From uncovering critical business decisions through historical case analysis to managing boardroom crises and designing strategies for 2047, participants must demonstrate business acumen, financial understanding, strategic thinking and leadership. Every decision carries consequences, every challenge demands adaptability, and every strategy shapes the future. Assemble your team of four and experience the journey from decoding business challenges to leading an organisation through uncertainty. ROUND 1A – THE TIMELINE TRIAL Assess the Past. Identify the Pattern. Teams will participate in an online assessment based on the business and economic history of Trikaal Industries. The assessment will test their understanding of the company's historical events, business decisions and financial developments. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Timeline-Based Assessment Evaluation: Business acumen, financial understanding and historical interpretation. ROUND 1B – THE CASE DOSSIER Uncover the Mistakes. Decode the Crisis. Following the assessment, teams will receive a confidential case dossier containing historical business records, financial exhibits and operational information related to Trikaal Industries. Participants must analyse the provided materials, identify the company's genuine strategic mistakes, uncover the underlying causes and recommend corrective actions supported by evidence. ROUND 2 – KAAL-SANKAT Survive the Present The mistakes from Round 1 become the starting point for a live boardroom crisis simulation. Teams will take charge of Trikaal Industries, with members assigned the roles of CEO, CFO, COO and CMO. Participants will face business dilemmas involving cash pressure, operational challenges, competitor threats and reputational risks. Every decision will impact key business metrics, requiring teams to balance financial performance, operational stability and strategic priorities. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline – On Campus, XAVIESTA 5.0, Day 2 Format: Role-Based Staggered Briefings + Decision Sheets Qualification: Top 6 Teams advance to the final Evaluation: Crisis Management, Financial Thinking, Leadership and Accountability. ROUND 3 – YUGPARIVARTAN Shape the Future The six finalists will move forward to 2047, inheriting business positions shaped by their Round 2 decisions. Teams must develop a future-ready strategy for Trikaal Industries covering business model, finance, technology, workforce, sustainability and risk. A surprise constraint will challenge their plans, followed by a boardroom presentation and jury Q&A. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline – Grand Finale, XAVIESTA 5.0, Day 2 Format: Strategy Build + Surprise Constraint + Boardroom Presentation + Jury Q&A Finalists: Top 6 Teams from Round 2 Evaluation: Strategic Vision, Innovation, Financial Viability and Boardroom Leadership. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Confidential Case Analysis + Written Submission Submission: Case analysis based exclusively on the provided dossier. Qualification: Top 16 Teams advance to Round 2. Evaluation: Business acumen, financial interpretation and problem identification. OVERALL RULES & REGULATIONS Team Size: 4 members per team across all rounds. No substitutions once registered. Eligibility: Open to all college students. Valid College ID is required for on-campus rounds. Structure: Round 1 (Online) → Top 16 Teams → Round 2 (Offline) → Top 6 Teams → Round 3 (Offline Grand Finale). Continuity: Outcomes carry forward between rounds. No team resets its position once a round concludes. Round 1: Based solely on the provided materials. Round 2 Roles:

description: Step into the shoes of founders and bring your entrepreneurial vision to life with NAVRACHNA, the flagship Shark Tank-style pitch competition at XAVIESTA 5.0. Designed to challenge innovation, business acumen and…
details_text: Step into the shoes of founders and bring your entrepreneurial vision to life with NAVRACHNA, the flagship Shark Tank-style pitch competition at XAVIESTA 5.0. Designed to challenge innovation, business acumen and financial thinking, the competition takes participants through three exciting stages: developing a compelling business pitch, presenting their venture before a panel of investors, and navigating real-world business crises. From identifying market opportunities and building viable business models to defending financial assumptions and making strategic decisions under pressure, participants must demonstrate creativity, adaptability and entrepreneurial excellence. Assemble your team of four and pitch your way from an idea to a venture ready to face the real world! ROUND 1 – THE PITCH DECK Build the Vision. Pitch the Idea. Teams must submit a written pitch deck presenting their entrepreneurial venture, including the problem being addressed, proposed solution, target market, value proposition, competitive advantage, growth strategy, financial assumptions and funding ask. The submission will be evaluated on innovation, problem-solution fit, market understanding and completeness. The Top 16 teams will qualify for Round 2. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Online on Unstop Format: Written Pitch Deck Submission: Business pitch deck covering problem, solution, target market, value proposition, competitive advantage, growth strategy, financials and funding ask. Qualification: Top 16 Teams Evaluation: Innovation, problem-solution fit, market understanding and completeness. ROUND 2 – THE FOUNDER'S PITCH Present the Vision. Defend the Business. Shortlisted teams will present their ventures before a panel of judges, explaining their business models, target markets, competitive positioning, financial assumptions, scalability and funding requirements. The round will consist of a live pitch followed by an investor-style cross-examination, where participants must defend their assumptions and demonstrate a strong understanding of their venture. This is a qualifying round and not the final. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline Format: Live Pitch + Investor Q&A Challenge: Present and defend the business model, market opportunity, competition, financials, scalability and funding ask. Evaluation: Business understanding, communication, financial thinking and ability to defend assumptions. Qualification: Finalists advance to Round 3. ROUND 3 – FACE THE REAL WORLD Adapt. Negotiate. Defend. Finalists will deliver a concise pitch or recap of their venture before facing a real-time, scenario-based cross-examination. Teams will encounter unexpected business challenges tailored to their ventures, including cost shocks, new competitors, cash-flow crises, sudden demand surges and regulatory changes. Participants must adapt their strategies, explain trade-offs and defend their decisions before the judging panel. Round Details: Team Size: 4 Members Mode: Offline – Grand Finale Format: Final Pitch/Recap + Scenario Challenge + Investor/Judge Cross-Examination Challenge: Real-world business crisis and strategic decision-making. Evaluation: Strategic thinking, adaptability, financial judgment, negotiation, communication, teamwork and founder mindset. OVERALL RULES & REGULATIONS Team Size: 4 Members. No substitutions once registered. Open to college students; valid ID is required for offline rounds. Format: Round 1 (Online) → Round 2 (Offline) → Round 3 (Offline Final). AI in Round 1: Language/design polishing only; not for the core business idea or financials. One laptop per team for offline presentation material; mobile phones are prohibited unless explicitly permitted. Submission deadlines and prescribed formats apply; no late submissions or resubmissions. No inter-team collaboration; violations may lead to disqualification. title: Robowars: Mahyem
organiser: Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology (TIET), Patiala
description: Event Description: A high-speed, head-to-head robotics competition where custom-built robots face off in a 1v1 mechanical soccer match. Teams design, build, and pilot their manual bots in a purpose-built arena to…
details_text: Event Description: A high-speed, head-to-head robotics competition where custom-built robots face off in a 1v1 mechanical soccer match. Teams design, build, and pilot their manual bots in a purpose-built arena to outmaneuver opponents, defend their penalty zones, and score goals using a mini football. Date: 21st November (Tech Inspection & Pool Stage) / 22nd November (Knockouts & Finals) Registration Fee: ₹800- per Team Registration Process: Participants will have to register on the official Saturnalia registration platform before the deadline mentioned on the platform. Participation may be subject to shortlisting in case of an overwhelming response. Only shortlisted participants, if applicable, will be notified about the further process. Participants must provide the required details and complete all necessary registration formalities within the specified deadline. Participation is exclusively open to college students possessing valid college ID cards for the current academic year. Participants must carry their valid college ID card during the event. The registration fee, if applicable, will be communicated through the official registration platform. Rules & Regulations: Event Overview & Arena Specifications: Mayhem is the premier combat robotics tournament of Saturnalia. Engineering teams design and build wireless combat machines that can deliver active kinetic strikes while withstanding hostile impacts. A robot wins by disabling its opponent through a Technical Knockout (TKO), or by scoring the most points for Aggression, Control and Damage. Arena Specifications & Containment: Enclosure Footprint: 16 ft × 16 ft × 7 ft fully enclosed steel frame High-impact, shatter-resistant polycarbonate safety walls Reinforced perimeter base guards Active Floor Hazard Pit: A 3 ft × 3 ft automated floor pit opens during the final 60 seconds of every match round. Forcing an opposing robot completely into the pit is an instant TKO. Safety & Containment Systems: Dual hard-wired emergency arena kill switches Optical containment screens Active smoke and exhaust ventilation for battery safety Weight Classes, Roster & Eligibility: Every machine must pass formal technical inspection before competing. Weight limits are strictly enforced, with a maximum tolerance of 1%. Weight Classes: Featherweight: up to 8.0 kg (17.6 lbs) Middleweight: up to 15.0 kg (33.0 lbs) Heavyweight: up to 30.0 kg (66.0 lbs) Roster & Structural Rules: Team Roster: 2 to 6 registered members per team. Teams may include members from more than one college, provided everyone’s student credentials are verified. Dimensions: there is no limit on overall dimensions. The fully assembled robot must fit through the 4 ft × 4 ft arena access hatch without disassembly. Walker Bonus: robots using true non-wheeled linear walking mechanisms get an extra 10% weight allowance above their class limit. Cluster Bots: a team may deploy multiple sub-units under one entry. The combined mass and dimensions of all active sub-units must stay within the class limits. Technical, Power & Weapon Regulations: Control Systems & Radio: Radio Protocol: 2.4 GHz digital spread-spectrum systems with frequency-hopping channels. Prohibited Control: tethered remote connections and fully autonomous robots are strictly prohibited. Fail-Safe Requirement: all drive systems and weapon throttles must return to neutral/zero power immediately if the transmitter signal is lost or interrupted. Electrical Power & Battery Shielding: Voltage Cap: electric drive systems only. The potential between any two electrical points must not exceed 36 V DC. Engines: internal combustion engines (ICE) are banned. Battery Containment: every LiPo, LiFe or gel battery cell must be fully enclosed in a rigid enclosure of at least 2 mm steel or aluminium plate, to contain thermal runaway. Mobility & Weapons: Allowed Mobility: Wheels Treads Walking mechanisms Controlled hopping assemblies (maximum height clearance of 6 ft) Prohibited Mobility: Vacuu

details_text: Date of Event: 23rd November 2026 Registration Fee: 150 per Participant Overview Every brand has a story, and some of them ended badly. Brand War hands teams a struggling or failed real-world brand and challenges them to bring it back to life, one round at a time. Teams rebuild the brand in stages: first the logo and tagline, then the campaign, and finally the social media strategy. After every round, the judges score the work and the lowest-scoring teams are eliminated. Only the strongest five teams reach the final pitch, and the top three of them take the podium. A surprise Plot Twist at the start of Round 2 changes the situation of the brand and tests how well teams adapt under pressure. The event brings together design thinking, marketing and storytelling. It rewards the team that understands why the brand failed, finds a fresh idea for it, stays strong round after round, and sells that idea convincingly. Eligibility: Open to all students of any branch and year. Teams of 2-3. Performance Guidelines: Each round is timed, and qualifying teams advance to the next one. description: Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate, postgraduate, and high school students, as well as working professionals and stock market enthusiasts. No prior finance or trading background is required; concepts are taught from…
details_text: Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate, postgraduate, and high school students, as well as working professionals and stock market enthusiasts. No prior finance or trading background is required; concepts are taught from absolute scratch. Format & Rules Mode: 2-Day Offline Workshop at IIT Bombay Campus. Duration: 12 to 16 Hours total (split across 2 days). Prerequisites: Participants must bring their own laptop (with internet capability), notepad, and pen. Team Structure: Participants must register individually. Inter-College & Inter-Specialization: Allowed for all hands-on group tasks and capstone exercises (participants from any college, stream, or academic background can collaborate). Certification: A Certificate of Training from Techfest, IIT Bombay will be awarded upon attending all sessions. Topics: Stock Market Fundamentals & Structure: Exchanges (NSE/BSE), market participants (FIIs, DIIs, Retail), order execution types, and index dynamics . Fundamental Analysis & Stock Screening: Decoding financial statements (P&L, Cash Flow), key ratios (P/E, ROE, Debt-to-Equity), and building screener filters. Technical Analysis & Chart Reading Basics: Dow theory, dynamic support/resistance, trendlines, and core candlestick patterns (Hammer, Engulfing, Doji). Key Indicators & Trading Signals: Moving averages (SMA vs. EMA), momentum indicators (RSI, MACD), and volume breakout validation. Trading Strategies & Market Psychology: Swing trading, momentum investing, long-term value selection, and emotional discipline. Risk Management & Capital Protection: Position sizing rules, risk-to-reward ratios, stop-loss strategy, and capital allocation. AI Tools for Smart Investors: Leveraging AI assistants (ChatGPT/Claude) for fast quarterly earnings summaries and news breakdown. Live Market Workshop & Mock Trading Simulation: Live breakdown of Nifty 50 stocks, chart setups, and an interactive group portfolio simulation. Speakers Industry practitioners and senior equity analysts with hands-on trading experience in live markets. (Formal mentor profiles and bios will be updated on the portal prior to the event session).

title: CyberPeace Foundation ISR Innovation Hackathon | Defence Intelligence Summit 2027
description: All that you need to know about CyberPeace Foundation ISR Innovation Hackathon | Defence Intelligence Summit 2027 Are you ready to build solutions that strengthen the future of digital intelligence and security?…
details_text: All that you need to know about CyberPeace Foundation ISR Innovation Hackathon | Defence Intelligence Summit 2027 Are you ready to build solutions that strengthen the future of digital intelligence and security? Shaastra 2027, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras, in collaboration with the CyberPeace Foundation , invites innovators, developers, AI/ML enthusiasts and content creators to participate in the ISR Innovation Hackathon , a flagship competition of the Defence Intelligence Summit 2027. The competition aims to tackle emerging challenges surrounding AI-generated disinformation, deepfakes and digital manipulation through technology and public awareness. About the Competition The hackathon features two tracks: Track 1: Agentic AI Tools (High Complexity) Build the agent that catches the fake. Develop an autonomous AI agent that monitors simulated social media, messaging and video feeds to detect deepfakes and AI-generated disinformation. Your solution should integrate multiple verification techniques, analyse evidence and generate explainable verdicts with confidence levels. Teams of up to 4 members. Submit a PPT/PDF abstract outlining your proposed solution. Shortlisted teams will demonstrate their working agents at the finale. Track 2: Creator Content (Creative Challenge) Make the reel that teaches the trick. Create an original 30-90 second reel, video or carousel that educates audiences on identifying digital manipulation and misinformation. Choose one theme: Emotional Manipulation Fake Experts Impersonation Manufactured Outrage Forward Before You Think Open to individuals or teams of up to 4 members. Entries can be submitted in any Indian language. Shortlisted participants will take on a surprise live creative brief at the finale. Competition Structure Round 1: Online Preliminary Round Submit your AI agent abstract (Track 1) or original social media content (Track 2). Entries will be evaluated on creativity, originality, accuracy and technical feasibility. Round 2: Offline Finale at IIT Madras The top 10 teams from each track (20 teams in total) will be shortlisted and invited to the IIT Madras campus for the finale. Track 1: Shortlisted teams will demonstrate their AI agents live against a fresh simulated multi-platform feed. Track 2: Shortlisted teams will take on a surprise live creative brief on stage. The finalists will showcase their solutions before a distinguished panel of judges from the CyberPeace Foundation and the defence and technology ecosystem. Key Dates Registrations Close: December 7, 2026 (6:00 PM IST) Doubt Clearance Session: December 10, 2026 Round 1 Submission Deadline: December 13, 2026 (6:00 PM IST) Offline Finale: January 3, 2027 Prizes & Recognition A total prize pool of ₹90,000 is up for grabs! 1st Prize: ₹45,000 2nd Prize: ₹30,000 3rd Prize: ₹15,000 Resources & Guidelines Track 1 participants will work with a simulated multi-platform feed. Live platform scraping and real personal data are not permitted. All submissions must be original. Track 1 solutions must operate within the provided sandbox. Track 2 must not use synthetic media depicting real, identifiable people. AI-generated media must be labelled. Political-party content and material unsafe for general audiences are prohibited. Participants below 18 must provide verified guardian consent. Winning technical systems may be required to be open-sourced. Ready to Make an Impact? Whether you're building an AI agent to detect digital deception or creating content to help people recognise manipulation, this is your opportunity to contribute to a safer digital ecosystem. Register now and be part of the CyberPeace Foundation ISR Innovation Hackathon at the Defence Intelligence Summit 2027!

details_text: Robo Sumo is where power, precision, and strategy collide! Robots must begin from their designated starting positions inside the ring. A robot will be considered out as soon as any part of it touches the floor outside the ring. Weapons, sharp edges, hazardous materials, or mechanisms designed to cause harm are strictly prohibited. If neither robot is eliminated within 5 minutes, the judges will determine the advancing robot based on: Aggression — consistent initiation of attacks or pushes. Strategy — effectiveness of tactics used to push the opponent or avoid being pushed. Control — ability to maintain precise control of movement and positioning. Rules: Participants must carry their college ID cards. Arrive at the venue at least 15 minutes before the event for check-in. details_text: Moneyball is a football-themed strategy and management event that combines football knowledge, player auctions, squad building, tactical planning, financial management and negotiation. The event consists of a preliminary qualification round followed by an auction, league stage, transfer market and knockout stage. Prize Pool: Rs. 6000 (Winner : Rs. 4000 + Runner-Up : Rs. 2000) Registration Fee: Rs. 200 Date: 10/12/2026 Event Structure: Preliminary Round (Quiz): Teams participate in a football-based quiz conducted through Mentimeter or pen-and-paper format to shortlist the Top 10 Teams . Player Auction: The shortlisted teams participate in a live football player auction and use their allocated purse to construct a squad of 11–15 players . Teamsheet & Formation: After completing the auction, each team submits its final teamsheet along with the formation in which they want their team to play. The organizing team then constructs the corresponding custom teams in EA SPORTS FC. Round 1 (League Stage): All 10 teams compete in a round-robin league format , where every team plays against every other team. Qualification: The Top 4 teams based on their league-stage performance qualify for the knockout stage. The remaining 6 teams are eliminated from the championship. Transfer Market: After Round 1, a transfer market opens. The Top 4 teams can bid for players belonging to the eliminated teams. The bottom 6 teams can negotiate and sell their players to the team offering the best value. Round 2 (Knockouts): The Top 4 teams play two semi-finals followed by the Grand Final using their updated squads after the transfer market. Best Negotiator Award: Among the eliminated 6 teams, the team that finishes the transfer market with the highest remaining purse wins the Best Negotiator Award. Match Simulation: All football matches will be simulated on EA SPORTS FC in CPU vs CPU mode at Legendary/Ultimate difficulty . Participants will not directly control the players during matches. Winner: The winner of the Grand Final will be declared the Moneyball Champion . Event Specific Rules: Each team must consist of 2-4 players . A team leader must be designated as the official point of contact for the team. The preliminary round will shortlist the Top 10 teams for the main event. Each qualified team will receive an equal starting purse for the player auction. Each team must construct a squad consisting of 11–15 players during the auction. Once the auction is completed, teams must submit their final teamsheet and preferred formation . All 10 qualified teams will participate in the Round 1 round-robin league stage . The Top 4 teams after Round 1 will qualify for the knockout stage. The remaining 6 teams will be eliminated from championship contention but will remain eligible for the Transfer Market and Best Negotiator Award . During the Transfer Market, qualified teams may bid for players belonging to eliminated teams. Eliminated teams have the right to negotiate and decide which offer provides the best value for their player. All transfers must be approved and recorded by the organizing committee before being considered official. Once the Transfer Market closes, no further player transfers will be permitted. The Top 4 teams will use their updated squads for the knockout stage. The knockout stage will consist of two semi-finals followed by a Grand Final . All matches will be simulated using EA SPORTS FC in CPU vs CPU mode . Matches will be played at Legendary/Ultimate difficulty , as determined by the organizing committee. Participants will not be permitted to control players during simulated matches. The winner of the Grand Final will be declared the Moneyball Champion . The eliminated team with the highest final purse after the Transfer Market will receive the Best Negotiator Award . Use of unfair means, manipulation of game settings, unauthorized changes to squads or deliberate exploitation of loopholes will result in disqualification. Judges' and organizing

description: CONNECT 2.0 – SHORT FILM COMPETITION Theme: Environmental Communication Objective: The competition encourages students to use filmmaking and storytelling to communicate environmental concerns, promote sustainability,…
details_text: CONNECT 2.0 – SHORT FILM COMPETITION Theme: Environmental Communication Objective: The competition encourages students to use filmmaking and storytelling to communicate environmental concerns, promote sustainability, and present innovative solutions. Eligibility: Open to college/university students across India. Participants may compete individually or in teams. Each team can have a maximum of 5 members. All team members must be enrolled students. Each participant can be part of only one film submission. Theme: Films must be based on Environment and Environmental Communication. Suggested topics include: Climate Change and Climate Action Water Conservation Waste Management and Recycling Plastic Pollution Biodiversity and Wildlife Forest Conservation Sustainable Living Environmental Justice Sustainable Agriculture Responsible Tourism Environmental Awareness Local Environmental Issues Films highlighting innovative solutions and positive environmental change are equally encouraged. Language: Films can be made in Gujarati, Hindi or English. Subtitles are permitted and must be clearly visible. Duration: Minimum: 3 minutes. Maximum: 10 minutes, including credits. Films exceeding the time limit may be disqualified. Film Format: Participants may submit fiction, documentaries, animation, short narratives, experimental films, mockumentaries or video essays. Originality and Copyright Films must be original creations of the participants. Plagiarism and unauthorised use of copyrighted material are strictly prohibited. Previously publicly released films are not permitted. Music, images and footage must be original, licensed or royalty-free. Use of AI AI tools may be used for supporting tasks such as editing, subtitles and sound enhancement. The core concept, storytelling and direction must be the participants' original work. Substantial AI-generated content must be disclosed during submission. Production Guidelines: Films may be shot using mobile phones, cameras or other recording equipment. No restriction on production budget. Participants must follow ethical filming practices and obtain necessary permissions. Technical Specifications: Preferred format: MP4. Recommended resolution: 1080p or higher. Clear audio and video quality are required. Opening and closing credits must mention the film title and team members. Submission Requirements: Participants must provide: Film Title Participant/Team Name College/University Name Team Leader's Contact Details Names of Team Members Film Synopsis Film Link/File Film Language AI-use declaration, if applicable Submission Deadline Films must be submitted through the official submission link. Late submissions may not be accepted. Submission dates will be announced soon. Screening and Rights: Selected films may be screened during CONNECT 2.0. Organisers may use film excerpts or stills for non-commercial event promotion, with appropriate credit. Original ownership remains with the creators. Disqualification: A film may be disqualified for: Violation of eligibility or duration criteria. Plagiarism or copyright infringement. False information or incomplete submissions. Violation of content guidelines. Substantial creation by someone other than the registered participants. General Guidelines: Participants are responsible for copyright permissions and the legality of their submissions. The organisers reserve the right to modify the schedule or competition arrangements. Any matter not covered under these rules will be decided by the organising committee. The decision of the judges and organising committee shall be final and binding. CONNECT 2.0 – Think Green. Tell Stories. Inspire Change.

title: GOVERNIA
description: What happens when a well-crafted policy proposal hits an unforeseen real-world crisis? GOVERNIA puts you and your team in the role of rival policy strategists competing to defend opposing economic and governance…
details_text: What happens when a well-crafted policy proposal hits an unforeseen real-world crisis? GOVERNIA puts you and your team in the role of rival policy strategists competing to defend opposing economic and governance frameworks. But winning isn't just about out-arguing your opponent—it's about how swiftly and intelligently you adapt when the ground shifts. No specialist knowledge of public policy or economics is required. The challenge rewards critical thinking, sharp observation, teamwork, and evidence-based adaptability. THE SCENARIO: THE DILEMMA Two opposing economic philosophies clash over public expenditure: Side A defends universal transfers to eliminate exclusion errors, while Side B advocates targeted assistance to conserve public resources. Midway through, a sudden macroeconomic shock forces both teams to overhaul their models under severe fiscal pressure.

title: CASE CLOSED: THE POLICY CRIME SCENE
description: Case Closed: The Policy Crime Scene puts you in the role of a Special Economic Forensics Officer investigating a fictional government programme that has gone wrong. Examine documents, crack codes, analyse financial…
details_text: Case Closed: The Policy Crime Scene puts you in the role of a Special Economic Forensics Officer investigating a fictional government programme that has gone wrong. Examine documents, crack codes, analyse financial records, connect conflicting statements and determine what actually happened. No specialist knowledge of economics or public policy is required. The challenge rewards observation, reasoning, teamwork and evidence-based conclusions. A fictional government programme received an allocation of ₹100 crore to improve school infrastructure. Records show that ₹72 crore was spent, while several schools claim that promised equipment never arrived. Officials maintain that the programme was implemented successfully. Something does not add up. Your mission is to determine: Where did the implementation process break down? Which records contradict one another? What can the evidence establish - and what remains unverified? What is the most defensible explanation for the failure? All figures, documents and allegations are fictional. A discrepancy alone does not prove fraud or establish individual wrongdoing.

details_text: In the world of business, one deal can change everything. But knowing which deal to make and how to make it, is what sets great strategists apart. THE ACQUISITION ARENA brings you into the world of mergers and acquisitions, where businesses look for opportunities to grow, gain an edge, and create value. Put yourself in the decision-maker's seat, evaluate the opportunities in front of you, and think through the challenges that come with making a deal. It's about looking beyond the numbers, understanding what makes a business valuable, and deciding whether an opportunity is worth pursuing. Bring your business sense, think on your feet, and show us how you'd approach a deal when the stakes are high. Every deal has two sides. Can you make the right move? Rules: Participants must report on time and follow all instructions issued by the organisers. The competition will consist of three rounds: THE DEAL ROOM, PRICE THE DEAL, and CLOSE THE DEAL. Participants must complete all case analyses, submissions, and presentations independently within the stipulated time. Plagiarism, collusion, or any unfair means will result in disqualification. Participants must adhere to the prescribed format and submission deadlines for each round. Judges will evaluate participants on strategic thinking, financial analysis, valuation, negotiation, and presentation skills. The organisers reserve the right to make necessary changes to the event schedule or rules. The judges' decisions regarding evaluation and final rankings will be final and binding.

details_text: IgniteCase – The Spark of Strategy IgniteCase is a business case-solving competition organised by E-Cell, Government College of Engineering, Amravati (GCOEA), as part of E-Sammelan'26. The competition is designed to test participants' analytical thinking, entrepreneurial mindset, logical reasoning and strategic decision-making. Through real-world-inspired business challenges, participants will identify problems, analyse situations and develop innovative, practical and growth-oriented solutions. The competition will be conducted through progressive stages: Competition Format: Initial Round: Online Qualifier – Case based quiz The opening round will be a timed online assessment featuring business-related questions and case-based MCQs. It will evaluate participants' entrepreneurial awareness, business fundamentals, logical reasoning, analytical ability and decision-making skills. Shortlisted teams will advance to the subsequent stages and will be directed for Offline Finals. Total Questions: 25 MCQs Total Marks: 50 Duration: 30 Minutes Question Format: Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) Eligibility: Open to students from all colleges and academic backgrounds. Students pursuing MBA, Business Analytics, Engineering, Medical, and other academic programmes are welcome. School Students and students pursuing higher studies are also eligible. Inter-college team participation is allowed. Team Structure: Minimum team size: 2 members. Maximum team size: 4 members. A team of 4 members is recommended. Guidelines and instructions: The online qualifying round will consist of 25 multiple-choice questions based on business awareness, entrepreneurship, logical reasoning, analytical thinking and business case scenarios. The total duration of the quiz will be 30 minutes. Each question will carry 2 marks, making the maximum score 50 marks. Participants must attempt the quiz within the given time limit. Each team must submit only one response through its registered team account. Team members may discuss and collaborate while attempting the quiz, but the submission must be made by the registered team representative. Participants are advised to ensure a stable internet connection before starting the quiz. Once the quiz begins, the timer will continue running. Participants should manage their time accordingly. Submissions made after the deadline or outside the prescribed platform will not be considered. Any form of unfair practice, impersonation or misuse of the competition platform may result in disqualification. Selection Criteria: Teams will be evaluated based on their total scores. In case of a tie, the time taken to complete the quiz may be considered as a tie-breaker, if supported by the platform. Shortlisted teams will be informed about the subsequent Guesstimate Challenge through their registered email addresses. The final selection for the on-campus stages will be based on the performance in subsequent rounds and the announced selection criteria. Important Note: This registration is for the initial online qualifier of IGNITECASE. Only shortlisted teams from the online round will progress to the subsequent stages.  Subsequent rounds will be conducted as per the qualification process.The Pre-Final and Final will be conducted offline at E-Sammelan'26, Government College of Engineering, Amravati. The competition celebrates innovative thinking and practical problem-solving, rewarding teams that can transform complex business challenges into impactful and sustainable solutions. Organised by: E-Cell, Government College of Engineering, Amravati (GCOEA)

title: Glideator
description: Overview The Glideator is a newly ideated event introduced for the first time at Shaastra 2026, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras. This exciting challenge is designed to test the stability, maneuverability,…
details_text: Overview The Glideator is a newly ideated event introduced for the first time at Shaastra 2026, the annual technical festival of IIT Madras. This exciting challenge is designed to test the stability, maneuverability, and control precision of RC gliders as they precisely navigate through a challenging obstacle course. Participants must rely solely on aerodynamic efficiency and pilot skill — without the aid of powered propulsion — to complete the course with maximum accuracy and control. Competition details: Round 0 - Preliminary Submission: 1) Video Demonstration Each participating team must submit a demonstration video showing : The Glider's control surfaces along with their movement while the glider is at rest. The glider has to be thrown from 3 - 5 metres height without any usage of the control surface and is expected to land safely after at least 10 metres distance. Land safely after a designated spot in a square of radius 2m. The video should consist of measuring the vertical and horizontal distance before and after the launch of the glider. This video demonstrates that the glider possesses sufficient control, maneuverability, and has appropriate range. 2) Technical PDF Submission A detailed technical document must be submitted containing: Glider dimensions and total weight along with a photo of the glider. (The dimensions of any other physical components that are used (like a carbon rod used as a spar) are to be mentioned.) Power source and other electronic components' specifications. Control surface dimensions. Thickness of the balsa wood used for the glider Place the photographs as proofs for each aspect mentioned. A hollow chamber of sufficient size should be arranged in the glider for adding weights in round 2. Round 1 — Glide ratio: Launch: Gliders should cover the greatest horizontal distance possible showcasing their aerodynamic efficiency. Teams must ensure their glider maintains a steady, level flight without erratic movements or stalls. In this round the glide ratio of each team's respective glider would be noted when released from a fixed spot. Round 2 — Obstacle Navigation: In this round, the glider should travel as far as it can and Specified landing zones were positioned at 2-meter intervals from the point of release. Teams were awarded additional points based on the zone in which the glider landed, with the condition that the entire glider must be contained within the designated zone to qualify for the corresponding points. Points were given for distance they travelled and also for landing in the specified zones. Additionally, teams were allowed to add weights (About 5gm each) provided by the organizing team to the glider, earning bonus points based on the number of weights successfully added. Rules and Guidelines Type: Glider(Without any propellor) only. Control System: Manual operation using a remote controller. Autonomous flight is not permitted. Dimensions: Wing span should be 70 - 75 cm and the other dimensions should be based on the wing span and aerodynamic parameters. Material to be used: Balsa wood of minimum thickness 3mm and maximum thickness 5 mm. Placing of foam or any other material between the balsa wood at wings or the body for strength or extra weight is strictly restricted. Stability & Maneuverability: The glider must demonstrate stable flight, precise low- altitude flight, and agile directional control. The weight of the glider should range between 350g and 500g. A hollow chamber of sufficient size should be arranged in the glider for adding weights in round 2. Important Dates: Registration Start: 28-10-2026 Registration Deadline: 10-12-2026 Main Event on: 03-01-2027 Venue: Student Activity Center (SAC), Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras Please go through the Problem statement attached below for all the details regarding the competition and for the submissions.

title: Roboceana 2027
description: ROBO OCEANA 2027 – Amphibious Rescue & Recovery Event Overview Robo Oceana 2027 challenges participants to design and operate a self-powered hovercraft capable of navigating land and water to complete a simulated…
details_text: ROBO OCEANA 2027 – Amphibious Rescue & Recovery Event Overview Robo Oceana 2027 challenges participants to design and operate a self-powered hovercraft capable of navigating land and water to complete a simulated flood-rescue mission. Teams must retrieve rescue payloads, overcome obstacles, and transport them safely to designated evacuation zones within the allotted time. Competition Structure Round 0 – Demonstration Teams must showcase their hovercraft's design and demonstrate its ability to maintain stability, navigate, and handle rescue payloads. Further submission guidelines will be announced by the organisers. Round 1 – Main Event Teams will operate their hovercraft in the physical arena to complete the rescue mission through the following stages: Land Navigation: Traverse smooth and rough surfaces and enter the water arena through one of two routes. Water Navigation: Avoid floating obstacles and navigate simulated currents while maintaining stability and control. Rescue & Recovery: Collect standard payloads (table tennis balls) and heavy payloads (golf balls). Evacuation: Return to land and deposit each payload in its designated rescue zone. Arena Specifications Land zone with smooth and rough surfaces. Sloped land-to-water transitions. Water zone with floating obstacles and simulated currents. Two entry routes: a short, narrow route with bonus points and a long, broad route. Designated payload collection and evacuation zones. Access gates that gradually close after a fixed duration. Technical Requirements Maximum dimensions: 50 × 40 × 40 cm Maximum weight: 4.5 kg Power: Completely self-powered. Battery: Insulated and securely enclosed. Control: RC operation permitted; physical tethers and external steering assistance prohibited. Rules & Penalties Follow all vehicle specifications and arena constraints. Deposit payloads into their respective rescue zones. Collisions, incorrect sorting, payloads falling outside designated zones, excessive instability, and exceeding payload limits may attract penalties. The team with the highest overall score in the main event will be declared the winner. In case of a tie, rescue efficiency, time performance, stability, and control may determine the final ranking.

title: Aerofloat Shaastra 2027
description: About the Event AeroFloat is an indoor lighter-than-air (LTA) vehicle competition held under the Aero Fest vertical of Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras . Teams will design, build, and fly a remotely controlled blimp .…
details_text: About the Event AeroFloat is an indoor lighter-than-air (LTA) vehicle competition held under the Aero Fest vertical of Shaastra 2027 at IIT Madras . Teams will design, build, and fly a remotely controlled blimp . Because blimps operate in a slow, buoyancy-dominated regime that is highly sensitive to control input, the competition tests both piloting precision and real-time combat strategy . Team & Venue Details Team Size: Up to 3 members per team . Participation Model: Open registration with an online technical check . Venue: Indoor venue at SAC Main Hall, IITM . Event Duration: 1 day . Competition Stages 1. Online Qualification Check Every registered team must submit a single continuous, unedited video demonstrating basic flight competency . The video must show an unassisted take-off, controlled climb and descent, controlled yaw, and an unassisted altitude hold with the vertical-thrust motor switched off . This round is evaluated on a pass/fail basis to grant an on-site Day 1 slot . 2. Round 1: Precision Navigation All blimps must pass a Day 1 technical check to ensure they meet limits, it must fit in a box of dimensions 1m * 0.5 m * 0.5m, helium gas only, a custom-built gondola, and a maximum total weight of 800 g . Teams pilot their blimp through a 3D course of up to 10 suspended hoops within a 3-minute time limit . The top 6 teams from the leaderboard advance to the Grand Finale . 3. Round 2: Aerial Combat (Grand Finale) The top 6 teams compete in a bracket-based, single-duel tournament inside a netted arena . The objective is to use a  5 cm standard pin to puncture the opponent's Mylar/BoPET envelope while protecting their own . A duel is won when the opponent's envelope is visibly punctured and loses lift . Key Rules & Requirements Build Rules: Envelopes must be commercially purchased, while the gondola and electronics must be built from scratch by the team . Propulsion & Control: The blimp must use electric motors with propellers and be controlled via a 2.4 GHz RC; autonomous flight is not permitted . Safety: Helium is the only permitted lifting gas; the use of hydrogen will result in strict and immediate disqualification . Combat Conduct: Ramming with the gondola or contacting an opponent's electronics during combat is prohibited and leads to immediate disqualification .

details_text: Embedded Programming Challenge (EPC 2027) The Embedded Programming Challenge is the flagship embedded systems event of Elecfest, IIT Madras, conducted under the Events and Workshops vertical of Shaastra 2027. It tests your expertise across digital design, low-level programming, microcontroller architecture, real-time systems and hardware interfacing, rewarding sharp problem-solving and clean implementation. Syllabus: Digital Logic & Verilog Low-Level Embedded C Microcontroller Assembly & ISA RTOS (FreeRTOS on ESP32) Peripherals & Communication Protocols Sensors & Interfacing Event Structure: The competition consists of two rounds. Round 1 is an online qualifier that tests theoretical knowledge of embedded systems. Round 2 is held on campus at IIT Madras and focuses on practical implementation and debugging. Details of Round 2 will be shared with qualified teams. Round 1: Duration: 1.5 hours Format: Online proctored quiz with MCQs, fill-in-the-blanks, error detection/missing-code and comprehension-based questions Qualification: Top 25 teams advance to Round 2 Marking Scheme: MCQs: +3, −1 Fill in the Blanks: +3, 0 Error Detection/Missing Code: +4, 0 (partial marking applicable) Comprehension: +1 per correct subpart Round 2: Duration: 3 hours Mode: Offline at IIT Madras (Old IE Lab) Teams will tackle 3–4 mandatory engineering challenges and one elective challenge of their choice. Datasheets and documentation for the components used will be shared beforehand. Solutions will be evaluated on functionality, component efficiency, optimisation, creativity and edge-case handling. Rules and Guidelines: Teams may have 1 or 2 members. A participant cannot be part of more than one team. Team members may be from different branches and/or colleges. In Round 2, teams may use at most one hint per question, up to half the total number of questions. The prescribed hint-earning mechanism applies to mandatory questions. Ties will be resolved using the published round-specific tie-breaker criteria. Participants must follow all instructions and deadlines set by the organisers. details_text: Overview: Are you interested in stock markets, trading strategies, and financial research? Here's your opportunity to put your knowledge to the test! Stocks Sena AlphaQuest 2026 is a pan-India competition designed for students passionate about financial markets, trading, and investment research. Organized by Stocks Sena, the competition challenges participants to test their knowledge, explore financial research tools, and experiment with trading strategies. About Stocks Sena: Stocks Sena is a stock market research platform built to make financial research more accessible and comprehensive. It brings together company financials, market-related news, portfolio tracking, and research tools to help users explore listed companies and financial markets. Discover Backtest Lab: One of the key features of Stocks Sena is Backtest Lab , which allows users to define trading strategy parameters and generate backtest reports showing how those strategies would have performed over a selected historical period. Participants can experiment with different parameters, evaluate historical strategy performance, and gain practical exposure to systematic trading strategy analysis. Competition Structure: The competition consists of three rounds: Round 1: Financial Markets Quiz Test your understanding of financial markets, fundamental analysis, valuation, technical analysis, and investing concepts. Round 2: The Stocks Sena Advantage Challenge Explore Stocks Sena's features and demonstrate your understanding of how the platform can support financial research and market analysis. Round 3: Backtest Lab Challenge Use Stocks Sena's Backtest Lab to test a trading strategy over a specified historical period and submit your results for evaluation. Cash Prizes: Compete for a total national cash prize pool of ₹15,000. All-India Rank 1: ₹10,000 All-India Rank 2: ₹3,000 All-India Rank 3: ₹2,000 Potential Internship Opportunities: The competition also offers an opportunity to stand out beyond the leaderboard. National podium finishers may be considered for potential internship opportunities with Stocks Sena , based on their performance, skills, and the company's requirements. This is an opportunity to showcase your understanding of financial markets, analytical abilities, and interest in financial research and technology. Who Can Participate? Students from colleges and universities across India who are interested in stock markets, financial research, investing, or trading strategies are encouraged to participate. Whether you're beginning your journey in financial markets or already have experience analyzing companies and trading strategies, AlphaQuest offers an opportunity to learn, experiment, and compete. Certificates: Participants who meet the competition's participation requirements will receive a digital participation certificate. Join the Challenge: Explore the markets. Test your strategies. Compete with the best student talent across India.

details_text: Objective Develop an innovative antenna solution in Simcenter FEKO for emerging applications. About the Contest ANTENNOVATE 2026 invites students to design innovative antennas in Simcenter FEKO for emerging wireless applications. Participants will develop, simulate, and optimize antenna designs for technologies such as 5G/6G, V2X communication, advanced sensing, or satellite systems, and present their work through performance metrics, radiation characteristics, and technical analysis. Challenge Develop and optimize an antenna in Simcenter FEKO for emerging applications such as 5G/6G, V2X communication, and advanced sensing systems. Your project should demonstrate target performance and measurable results through electromagnetic simulation and analysis. Registration All participants must fill out the registration form and join the WhatsApp group provided in the form. Guidelines The project must be developed entirely in Simcenter FEKO, including antenna modeling, simulation setup, parameter definition, optimization if used, result visualization, and performance validation. Submissions must be original. If you reference an existing antenna design, research paper, or industry-standard topology, cite the source and clearly describe your modifications, improvements, or implementation approach. Clearly specify: Target application such as 5G/6G, V2X, satellite communication, radar, IoT, or sensing. Operating frequency or frequency range. Antenna type and configuration. Key design constraints and objectives. Provide simulation details including: Materials and substrate properties, if applicable. Feed mechanism and excitation parameters. Boundary conditions and solver settings. Assumptions made during modeling and analysis. Final submissions should demonstrate how the design addresses a real-world wireless or electromagnetic challenge and include technical analysis supported by FEKO simulation results. Submissions A submission form will be circulated close to the submission date. Upload a single ZIP file containing: .out file (Antenna model file) .cfx file (pre-processing) .pfs file (post-processing) YouTube video link (Demo and explanation) PowerPoint presentation Report covering the summary, methodology, assumptions, and key results File naming format: Name_College_ANT_FEKO.zip Eligibility Open to individual students. Original submissions only. Prizes Total Prize Pool: ₹25,000 in merchandise 1st Prize: ₹15,000 2nd Prize: ₹6,000 3rd Prize: ₹3,000 Important Dates Contest Duration: 29 October 2026 to 06 December 2026 Registration Deadline: 20 November 2026 Download Software Free Academic License for students (not institutions). Activate the software. Note: Only students with a college-domain email address can download the software. Resources FEKO YouTube Playlist: Altair How-to FEKO E-Learning: Getting Started with FEKO

title: Call for Papers: The Arthniti 2026-27
description: About: The Arthniti (ISSN: 2277-1344) is the official peer-reviewed research journal of the Department of Economics at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai. The journal features research papers and articles written by…
details_text: About: The Arthniti (ISSN: 2277-1344) is the official peer-reviewed research journal of the Department of Economics at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai. The journal features research papers and articles written by undergraduate students of economics and related disciplines. Every year, the journal publishes research on a specific theme, enriching the scope and suggesting a refreshing strand of thought to pick upon by the students every year across the disciplines of Economics, Finance, Political Science, Psychology, Technology, inter alia, and this year The Arthniti invites abstracts on the theme ‘Emergence’. Theme: Emergence is the process by which interactions among simple underlying components can give rise to complex behaviours and structures. Often, the ultimate outcome observed is neither intuitive nor reducible to those individual components. This theme looks at interdisciplinary ideas as emerging concepts that rarely respect the boundaries of a single field. Emergence therefore, is not merely change, but it further examines what change produces. An understanding of these processes is therefore imperative to not only navigating uncertainty but also building systems that are resilient to adapting for what comes next. This year, The Arthniti tries to capture the essence of its theme, ‘Emergence’ through diverse research papers. Instructions: This post is a call for paper submissions, that is, a complete research paper of up to 6000 words (excluding References and the Appendix) has to be submitted for the entry to be considered. The paper submissions have to adhere to the following guidelines: All in-text citations, references, tables figures, and depictions to be in the American Psychological Association (APA) 7 format and accurately numbered. The font must be Times New Roman with font size as 12. The paper must follow the following structure: • Abstract: A summary of the entire study, including the methods, findings and future outlook under 300 words. • Introduction: A brief overview of the background of your research study, a brief outline of the various fundamental elements that constitute the phenomenon you seek to explain. • Literature Review: A comprehensive review of literature surrounding the chosen subject, using any method of review. • Objectives: The various steps/methods/processes used as part of the study in answering the research question, in brief. • Hypothesis: The primary and secondary research questions that the author of the study seeks to answer, including the hypothesised relationship between the variables of the study. • Methodology: An exhaustive overview of the methods, datasets, models, processes that have been utilised in your research paper. • Policy Recommendations (if applicable): Actionable and empirical policy implications of your study. • Limitations: A transparent declaration of the pitfalls that you encounter in the process, or any information that hampers the validity or scope of the claims being made by the study. • Conclusion: A brief summary of the study. Since the journal is ISSN-indexed, all submissions made must be exclusive to The Arthniti, and any duplicate papers will be regarded as plagiarism. The journal maintains stringent academic standards, and any plagiarism or AI-generated textual usage will lead to disqualification of the submission. Note: Please submit your entries through this form link.

title: MindShift - The Science of Decisions
description: Overview: Why do we remember some things and forget others? How does the brain shape our perception, behaviour and decisions? MindShift is a three-round competition exploring neuropsychology, cognition and human…
details_text: Overview: Why do we remember some things and forget others? How does the brain shape our perception, behaviour and decisions? MindShift is a three-round competition exploring neuropsychology, cognition and human behaviour. Through application-based challenges, scientific research and problem-solving, participants will investigate how cognitive processes influence the way we think and interact with the world. Designed for curious minds across disciplines, MindShift encourages scientific reasoning, critical thinking and evidence-based decision-making. No prior specialisation in neuroscience or psychology is required. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from all academic disciplines. Participants may register individually or in teams of 1–4 members. Competition Rounds Round 1: Brain Basics | Online Quiz An application-based quiz covering foundational concepts in memory, attention, perception, learning, cognitive biases and decision-making. Questions will focus on applying concepts to real-world scenarios rather than relying solely on factual recall. A preparatory reference document will be provided before the round, making it accessible to beginners. Round 2: NeuroDesign | Submission Round Shortlisted participants will receive a challenge brief requiring them to approach an unfamiliar neuropsychological problem through scientific reasoning, research and creative problem-solving. Teams must develop a structured response, justify their approach and consider its feasibility within the given constraints. The challenge will run over two days, with detailed instructions, deliverables and evaluation criteria released at the start of the round. Final Round: Offline Finale | IIT Madras The finalists will participate in an interactive, research-driven neuropsychology challenge at IIT Madras on 2 January 2027 . Teams will investigate a neuropsychological condition, explore its underlying mechanisms using credible scientific literature, and develop an evidence-informed solution or intervention concept. Teams will submit their research and proposed approach with appropriate citations and present their findings to a judging panel. Detailed task requirements and evaluation criteria will be shared with the finalists. Evaluation Criteria: Participants will be evaluated on scientific understanding, analytical reasoning, research quality, creativity, feasibility, problem-solving and communication. Detailed, round-specific judging criteria will be communicated to participants. Prizes Total Prize Pool: ₹35,000 Winner certificates will be provided in hard copy. Finalist and participation certificates will be provided digitally. Why Participate? Explore the science behind human cognition, engage with scientific research and tackle challenging problems that go beyond conventional quizzes. Develop skills in research, critical thinking, scientific communication and teamwork while investigating the fascinating relationship between brain function and behaviour. Think critically. Investigate the evidence. Discover the Science of Decisions.

title: Petri Dish Challenge
description: Overview: Beyond the naked eye lies a universe of chaos, beauty, and hidden potential. Are you ready to decode it? The Petri Dish Challenge invites budding microbiologists to identify an unknown bacterial culture using…
details_text: Overview: Beyond the naked eye lies a universe of chaos, beauty, and hidden potential. Are you ready to decode it? The Petri Dish Challenge invites budding microbiologists to identify an unknown bacterial culture using standard microbiological techniques. Participants will explore bacterial isolation and culture, Gram staining, biochemical tests and antibiotic susceptibility testing. They must analyse experimental data, draw scientific conclusions and present their findings clearly. The event consists of an online quiz round followed by an offline laboratory round at IIT Madras. Participants will be shortlisted for the final round based on their performance in the online round. Target Audience: Students interested in: Microbiology and microbial identification Biotechnology and biomedical sciences Wet-lab techniques, bacterial culture and biochemical analysis Experimental reasoning and scientific interpretation Eligibility: Undergraduate and postgraduate students from all disciplines, including engineering, science, medical, arts, commerce, management and law. Format: Round 1: Online Quiz Platform: Unstop Format: Online quiz covering biotechnology, microbiology and microbiology laboratory techniques Structure: Approximately 30–40 questions Dates: December 12-13,2026 Participants must attempt at least one quiz to be considered for qualification to the offline final round. Final Round: Offline at IIT Madras Location: UG Labs, IIT Madras Dates: January 4–5, 2027 Participants will receive an unknown bacterial sample and conduct laboratory investigations, including: Staining and cell morphology, including cotton blue staining Cell count and viable cell determination Antibiotic susceptibility testing and Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) Lactose fermentation and extracellular enzyme activity/synthesis Motility testing and biochemical characterisation The final round includes hands-on experiments, lab report preparation, live presentations and a viva. Evaluation Criteria: Selection and execution of appropriate laboratory tests Accuracy of observations, recordings and interpretation Scientific reasoning and evidence supporting bacterial identification Quality and clarity of the lab report and presentation Performance during the viva examination

details_text: NITRO GP is an adrenaline-fuelled, nitro-powered RC car racing championship hosted at Shaastra, bringing together hobbyists, students, and professional racers from across India to enjoy the thrills of navigating challenging turns, ramps, and rugged terrain in a test of speed, precision, and control. The competition celebrates creativity, engineering expertise, technical craftsmanship and sharp reflexes, pushing both the machines and their drivers to their limits. Competition details: VIDEO SUBMISSION: Each team must submit a clear video showcasing their car's composition, functionality, and performance on a test track. The video should highlight that it is a 1:8 Nitro fuel-based RC car which is functional.It must be submitted before the deadline for evaluation and shortlisting. QUALIFIERS: All teams have to go through a 3-lap time trial round. Each driver’s fastest time in this qualifying round will be considered. The Top 16 proceed to the next round and are slotted according to their positions in this round. ROUND ROBIN: The teams are split into 4 groups and race among themselves in the group. The top 2 of each group directly proceed to the next stage, whereas the third-place team of each group goes into a revival round. REVIVAL: The 3rd-place teams race each other where the first-place team also advances to the semifinals. QUARTER-FINALS: 9 teams are seeded and race out of which 6 teams head to the semifinals. SEMI - FINALS: 2 high-stakes races of 3 cars each; the top 2 of each race proceed to the finals. FINALS: Teams that qualify from the semi-finals will advance to the final race. The final race will be of longer duration.Pit stops are available. Grid positions for the final will be based on the number of laps completed in the semi-final (in the given time). Rules & Guidelines: Open only to Nitro fuel-based 1:8 RC buggies; further specifications regarding the cars are mentioned in the PS. Further rules and guidelines are available in the Problem Statement.

details_text: CTF Website Registration All participants must register through the official CTF platform using the link below.
