Compete in a team and explore challenges across web exploitation, cryptography, digital forensics, reverse engineering, OSINT, steganography, and more. Uncover hidden flags, piece together clues, and navigate an unfamiliar digital world through problem-solving, creativity, and technical skills. Whether you're an experienced cybersecurity enthusiast or a beginner curious about ethical hacking, there's a challenge waiting for you! CTF Website Registration All participants must register through the official CTF platform using the link below. CTF Website: https://dead-drop-ctf-six.vercel.app/ Guidelines Eligibility: Open to students from any college. Participation Format: Team-based participation. Team size must follow the limits specified by the organizers. Challenge Categories: Web exploitation, cryptography, digital forensics, reverse engineering, OSINT, steganography, and other cybersecurity-related challenges. Event Duration: Six hours of active CTF gameplay, with a 30-minute break during which the competition will be paused. Schedule: 11:30 AM: Check-in, introduction, and team settlement. 12:00 PM: CTF begins. During the day: 30-minute break; the CTF timer is paused. 6:30 PM: CTF ends and final scores are verified. Identity Verification: All participants must carry a valid college ID card for verification. Requirements: Each team must bring its own laptop(s) and charger(s). Scoring: Teams earn points by successfully solving challenges and submitting the correct flags. Final scores will be verified by the organizers. Rules Punctuality: Participants must report to the venue by 11:30 AM. Late entries will not be permitted. Competition Duration: The CTF begins at 12:00 PM and ends at 6:30 PM, including a 30-minute break during which gameplay is paused. Identity Verification: A valid college ID card is mandatory for every participant. Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptops and chargers. Authorized Targets Only: Teams may attack and investigate only the challenges and systems explicitly provided for the CTF. Attacking other teams, external systems, or the competition infrastructure is strictly prohibited. Flag Confidentiality: Flags and solutions must not be shared outside the registered team or posted publicly until the event concludes. Fair Play: Teams must solve challenges independently. Unauthorized collaboration, plagiarism, or attempts to manipulate the scoring system may result in disqualification. Respectful Conduct: Harassment, abusive behavior, or deliberate disruption of other participants or organizers will result in disqualification. Scoring Disputes: Any concerns regarding challenge validation, flag acceptance, or final scores must be reported to the organizers during the event or before final results are declared. The organizers' decision on scoring disputes will be final.

details_text: Overview – Trust No One. Question Everything. AUDACIA 2026 | 11th Integrity & Ethics Conclave | Symbiosis Centre for Information Technology (SCIT), Pune Description In a boardroom where everyone has an agenda, can you really trust the person sitting next to you? Welcome to THE UNSEEN HAND, an exciting offline corporate social-deduction challenge inspired by the popular game Among Us, where business strategy meets mystery, deception, and unexpected twists! Imagine stepping into a corporate boardroom where critical decisions must be made, challenges arise without warning, and every individual appears to be working toward a common objective. But appearances can be deceiving. Behind professional conversations and convincing arguments, hidden motives and conflicting interests may be at play. As situations evolve and uncertainty grows, participants must rely on their observation, strategic thinking, communication, and decision-making abilities to navigate the boardroom. Will you recognize the warning signs before it's too late? Can you distinguish a genuine ally from someone quietly influencing the outcome? In this boardroom, every decision matters, every conversation counts, and trust might be your greatest strength or your biggest vulnerability. Get ready for a game where corporate intelligence meets psychological strategy, and nothing is quite as straightforward as it seems! Be prepared to collaborate with unfamiliar faces, build new alliances, and adapt to an unpredictable boardroom environment. Competition Format Mode: Offline Venue: SIC Campus, Pune Enter the Boardroom The Unseen Hand places participants in a simulated corporate environment where they must navigate business challenges, interpret information, collaborate with others, and make decisions under uncertainty. The competition combines elements of: Corporate Strategy and Decision-Making Social Deduction and Observation Communication and Persuasion Logical and Critical Thinking Teamwork and Adaptability Crisis Response and Problem-Solving Participants will encounter evolving challenges that test their ability to balance strategy, judgment, and trust. Expect the Unexpected! In the corporate world, the most important developments are not always announced in advance. The Unseen Hand embraces this uncertainty through unexpected scenarios, shifting circumstances, and challenges that demand quick thinking. There's more to this boardroom than meets the eye! Certain aspects of the gameplay will remain confidential until the event to preserve fairness, suspense, and the element of surprise. Participants should be prepared to demonstrate: Strategic Thinking & Decision-Making: The ability to evaluate situations, consider alternatives, and make informed decisions under pressure. Observation & Analytical Reasoning: The ability to recognize inconsistencies, interpret information, and identify important details in complex situations. Communication & Persuasion: The ability to communicate ideas, question assumptions, and present convincing arguments. Adaptability & Collaboration: The ability to work with unfamiliar participants, respond to unexpected developments, and navigate changing circumstances. Specific scoring mechanisms and challenge-wise evaluation criteria will be communicated by the organizers as applicable. Poor Social Conduct, Misbehaviour, Foul/abusive Language, Unsportsmanlike Conduct, or Intentional/reckless Damage to Campus Property or The Race Arena.

details_text: About AdVenture AdVenture is a three-round marketing and brand strategy competition conducted as part of Strategia 2027. The event places participants in the role of an advertising and marketing agency, challenging them to develop, defend, and adapt a campaign for a real product from a real brand. The competition tests participants’ ability to understand consumers, identify market opportunities, think creatively, and make strategic decisions under pressure. Across three progressively challenging rounds, teams will develop a campaign strategy, respond to a marketing crisis affecting the same brand, and defend their decisions in an undisclosed live finale. Focus Areas Consumer Insight Brand and Market Relevance Creative Thinking Strategic Thinking Problem Diagnosis Who Can Participate? Any undergraduate (UG) or postgraduate (PG) student currently pursuing their education is eligible to participate. Team Size and Format Team Composition: 2 members. Solo entries are not permitted. Event Format: 3 rounds. Preliminary Rounds: 2 online rounds. Final Round: Offline. Rounds and Competition Structure Round 1: Pulse Check: The Brief (Online) The real product and brand for the case will be announced at the beginning of the round. Teams must develop a campaign concept for the given brand. Participants must submit either a slide deck (PPT/PDF) or a single poster, strictly following the format specified in the round brief. The highest-performing teams, with the number to be announced, will advance to Round 2. Round 2: The Red Alert: Crisis (Online) Teams will receive a marketing crisis or product-related problem connected to the same brand and case used in Round 1. The crisis may involve a public relations setback, declining brand relevance, a repositioning requirement, or a failed product launch. Teams must diagnose the problem and develop a revamped marketing brief containing: Problem Diagnosis and a Fresh Strategic Direction Key Messaging and a Proposed Course of Action This round evaluates the ability to respond to unexpected challenges, rethink campaign strategies, and propose practical, relevant solutions while maintaining brand alignment. Round 3: The Full Throttle (Offline) The final round will be an undisclosed surprise challenge, revealed only when the round begins. Finalists must think on their feet and defend the campaign developed in Round 1 and the crisis response developed in Round 2 before the judging panel. This round tests strategic clarity, adaptability, confidence, and the ability to justify marketing decisions under pressure. The AdVenture Challenge AdVenture goes beyond conventional marketing exercises by challenging participants to think like real-world brand strategists. From building a compelling campaign to navigating a brand crisis and defending their decisions in a live finale, teams must demonstrate creativity backed by strategic reasoning. Bring your ideas, challenge conventions, and prove that you can turn a brand brief into a winning strategy. AdVenture: Brand. Buzz. Boom.

details_text: Official Competition Guidelines Theme: The Things We Don’t Question Organized Collaboratively by: D-LAB, Design Community (IISER Berhampur) with Art Clubs of Other IISERs Overview & Thematic Brief: We navigate daily life governed by unexamined habits, systemic norms, invisible social defaults, and unquestioned cultural agreements. ARTICULATE invites designers to interrogate the familiar challenging viewers to pause, reflect, and ask critical questions about the everyday realities we take for granted. The Theme: The Things We Don't Question: The Things We Don’t Question: Use the medium of graphic design to explore an assumption, belief, behaviour, practice, or system that has become so familiar that we rarely stop to question it. Your poster should make the familiar feel unfamiliar, something that makes people pause, think, and question what they usually take for granted. ARTICULATE invites thinkers, illustrators, graphic designers, and creative minds across India to disrupt this visual complacency. Your artboard is an analytical instrument to surface hidden paradoxes, challenge accepted defaults, and construct visual metaphors that make viewers reconsider their everyday assumptions. Thematic Scope & Satirical Commentary / Critiques: Prohibition on Use of Direct Personalities & Real-World Entities’ Identities. Critique must remain systemic, structural, and conceptual. Use allegory, generic archetypes, visual metaphors, and symbolic representation rather than literal real-world identities. Submissions must maintain ethical design standards, completely avoid personal attacks, hate speech, or defamation, and channel their visual commentary into universal, thought-provoking ideas. Design Specifications & Technical Requirements: Format & Dimensions: Submissions must be exactly A4 size (portrait orientation recommended). Quantity: One original poster submission per registered participant. Thematic Alignment: Every submission must demonstrate a rigorous, creative, and critical interpretation of the theme, The Things We Don't Question. Submission Deliverables: Participants must compile and submit all three mandatory deliverables via the official registration portal: High-Resolution Poster Image: One export in JPG, JPEG, or PNG format (minimum 300 DPI recommended). Source / Editable Design File: The original editable working file in PSD, AI, SVG, or other industry-standard formats. For designs authored in Canva, an unrestricted editable or template share link must be provided. Portfolio & Concept Document (PDF): A single PDF containing: A full-page high-resolution preview of the poster. A structured written rationale (up to 250 words) articulating the conceptual premise, creative methodology, design iterations, and social or moral values reflected within the artwork. Mandatory Social Engagement & Verification: To ensure transparent public exhibition and complete validation of participation, entrants must fulfill all of the following steps prior to the deadline: Follow @design_iiserbpr on Instagram. Post the finalized poster on Instagram as a Collaborator Post with @design_iiserbpr. Include the concept rationale / artist statement within the post caption or in the post itself. Tag the following institutional and partner accounts in the caption: @design_iiserbpr @artclub_iisertirupati Note: Collaboration acceptance and tagging of all partner entities are compulsory requirements for jury review. Prizes & Rewards (Total Prize Pool: ₹10,500) The competition offers a comprehensive prize pool valued at ₹10,500, distributed across direct cash rewards, Amazon gift vouchers, and official honors: Overall Prize Pool: ₹10,500 (inclusive of Cash Prizes & Amazon Gift Vouchers). 1st Place (Winner): ₹3,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence 2nd Place (First Runner-Up): ₹2,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence 3rd Place (Second Runner-Up): ₹1,000 + Amazon Vouchers / Certificate of Excellence Special Mentions (3 Positions): ₹500 eac

details_text: MOLEQUEST Case Challenge is a competition for people who love to read, think and connect the dots. Teams (1-4 members) will dive into biological puzzles, work out what’s happening at the molecular level, and build solutions that hold up when the evidence takes an unexpected turn. The event is structured in three rounds, each one testing a progressively deeper layer of scientific competence: conceptual knowledge, analytical depth and real-time adaptability. The theme is Epigenetics. So, think like scientists and find what the epigenome is hiding. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students Target Audience: Students interested in Epigenetics and Genomics Molecular Biology Biotechnology Biochemistry Biomedical Engineering Plant and Agricultural biotechnology Competition Rounds: Round 1: Online Quiz This quiz will test grasp of basic molecular biology and epigenetics fundamentals, the toolkit you will need to crack the cases ahead. Be prepared to think fast and be sharp to earn your place in the next round. Round 2: Submission Round In this round, teams will be given a set of cases. Teams pick one of the cases, study the data provided, and submit a written report, answering the questions given in the case document. Finals at IIT Madras: Offline Round Teams arrive with a prepared PPT based on their Round 2 work and will be given a sealed envelope revealing new findings. They are then given 1 hour to rework their PPT adding any changes in their reasoning. They should then defend their Round 2 report and explain what changes and doesn’t change in their reasoning because of the new information to a panel of judges.

title: RoboRun 2027

details_text: All that you need to know about Robo Run Guidelines: A team shouldn't contain more than 5 members. Bot Dimensions:  Smaller than 20 * 20  cms. Participants are required to build an autonomous (not to be operated by a remote controller) line follower Bot, which can reach the end point of a maze in the shortest possible time. ( The line thickness will be 3-4 cm) Video submission round: This will be a submission round! You will have to prepare a small maze with two curves and show your line-following bot running on it. Shoot a video clip and attach the file. Round -1: In round 1, every team will be given a chance to run through the maze. The top set of teams will be qualified to final round. Shortlisting will be done based on the points you acquire. Refer to the problem statement for scoring criteria. Round -2: In round 2, the maze will additionally contain yellow blocks (10cm*10cm*10cm) directly placed on top of yellow squares. These yellow blocks are to be displaced from the square. The sqaures will act as a checkpoint only if the block is displaced completely. The maze and scoring pattern will be different between the two rounds. Robo Run Description: A Bot shall not be larger in length or width than 20 cm. There are no restrictions on the height of a Bot. A Bot should essentially comprise a drive motor to move it; a steering and turning method; sensors to detect the maze turns; sensors to ignore the action of the rest Bots and a source to provide power. A Bot shall be self-contained (no remote controls). A Bot shall not use an energy source employing a combustion process. Required sensors may be used for identifying the block and the maze line. A Bot shall not leave any part of its body behind while navigating the maze. A Bot shall not jump over, fly over, climb, scratch, cut, burn, mark, damage, or destroy the line of the maze. Judges can debar any machine if it is likely to cause damage to the maze in any way. title: BREAKING BID : Presented by MARG The Management Society of Ram Lal Anand College
description: Competition Description Step into the world of strategy, business, and decision-making, where every choice has consequences and every move can create an opportunity. This competition challenges participants to think…
details_text: Competition Description Step into the world of strategy, business, and decision-making, where every choice has consequences and every move can create an opportunity. This competition challenges participants to think critically, understand market dynamics, and make strategic decisions under pressure. Combining a knowledge-based quiz with an immersive bidding and brand-building challenge, it tests both conceptual understanding and practical business acumen. Participants will progress through two rounds, moving from testing their knowledge and reasoning to applying their skills in a competitive business simulation. Think strategically. Bid wisely. Build intelligently. Round 1: Online Quiz The first round is an elimination-based online quiz designed to assess participants' knowledge, logical reasoning, analytical thinking, and decision-making abilities. The quiz will feature a diverse mix of questions covering business and economics concepts, marketing psychology, consumer behaviour, logical reasoning, and real-world business scenarios. Participants will be required to go beyond theoretical knowledge, interpret situations, identify patterns, and choose appropriate solutions under time constraints. Format: 20 questions 30-minute duration Multiple-choice, logical reasoning, and scenario-based questions No negative marking One attempt per team Performance in this round will determine qualification for the next stage. Round 2: The Bidding Challenge The second round takes participants into a competitive business simulation where strategic thinking, resource allocation, and calculated decision-making become essential. Teams will receive a fixed amount of virtual capital and compete to acquire business assets through a bidding process. Each asset offers distinct advantages and trade-offs, requiring participants to balance their ambitions with their available resources. Using their acquired assets, teams must develop a viable business, establish their market positioning, and demonstrate how their resources work together to create a competitive advantage. The challenge extends beyond bidding, requiring teams to justify their decisions, manage constraints, and respond strategically to unexpected market developments. The objective is not simply to acquire the most expensive assets, but to make intelligent investments and build a business capable of succeeding in a competitive market. Teams will be evaluated on their strategic decisions, resource management, business viability, adaptability, and overall performance. Rules and Regulations Participants must register in teams of 3–4 members. Each participant may be part of only one team. Qualification for the offline round depends on performance in the online quiz. Each team is permitted one quiz attempt, submitted by a designated team member. The online quiz must be completed within the stipulated time and in a single sitting once started. No negative marking will apply to the online quiz. Shortlisted teams must participate in the offline round according to the instructions provided by the organisers. During the bidding challenge, teams must operate within their allocated virtual capital. Borrowing and transferring credits between teams are not permitted. Teams must comply with the bidding rules, asset-acquisition requirements, and evaluation criteria communicated before the offline round. Any misconduct, plagiarism, or use of unfair means may result in disqualification. Participants must carry a valid college ID for the offline round. The organisers' and judges' decisions regarding evaluation and competition outcomes will be final and binding.

description: Have a research idea, an innovative solution, or findings worth sharing with the world? Aven Journal by Kartexa invites research paper submissions across multiple disciplines. A nonprofit publishing initiative by…
details_text: Have a research idea, an innovative solution, or findings worth sharing with the world? Aven Journal by Kartexa invites research paper submissions across multiple disciplines. A nonprofit publishing initiative by Kartexa, Aven Journal aims to make scholarly publishing more accessible by offering a platform where contributors can share their research and readers can access published work for free. Whether you are a student writing your first research paper, an independent researcher exploring a new idea, a professor advancing academic knowledge, a teacher sharing educational research, or an organization presenting research findings, we welcome your contribution. Our vision is simple: make research accessible, encourage knowledge sharing, and give ideas a platform to grow. Who Can Participate? The call for papers is open to: School and college students Undergraduate and postgraduate students Research scholars Independent researchers Professors and academic faculty Teachers and educators Colleges, universities and academic institutions Research organizations and other eligible organizations Institutional affiliation is not mandatory for independent researchers. Research Areas: We welcome original research and scholarly contributions in relevant disciplines, including: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Computer Science and Information Technology Engineering, Robotics and Emerging Technologies Natural and Applied Sciences Mathematics and Statistics Education and Learning Sciences Business, Economics and Management Social Sciences and Humanities Environmental Studies and Sustainability Agriculture and Interdisciplinary Research Submissions must fall within the journal's scope and comply with its editorial and publication policies. Types of Submissions: Depending on subject suitability and the journal's editorial policies, contributors may submit: Original research papers Review articles Interdisciplinary research Case studies Applied research Research-based technical papers Why Submit to Aven Journal? Free Publication There are no manuscript submission or publication fees. Free Public Access Published articles are available to readers without subscription or access charges. Inclusive Research Community Students and independent researchers can participate without requiring a university affiliation. Cross-Disciplinary Knowledge Sharing Contribute research across science, technology, education, humanities and other relevant disciplines. Accessible Research Records Published articles can have dedicated article pages with author attribution, abstracts, keywords and citation information, according to the journal's publication workflow. Submission Guidelines: Before submitting: Prepare an original manuscript relevant to the journal's scope. Include the title, abstract, keywords, author details and references. Ensure that all listed authors have approved the submission. Include applicable research ethics approvals and conflict-of-interest information. Follow the official author guidelines. Submit your manuscript through the official journal submission process. All submissions are subject to editorial screening and the journal's applicable review process. Submission does not guarantee acceptance or publication. Read the author guidelines and current publication policies before submitting.

title: EO Mumbai Global Student Entrepreneur Awards 2026
description: The EO Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (EO GSEA) is the premier event for student entrepreneurs worldwide. Student entrepreneurs compete against their peers from around the world in a series of local competitions to…
details_text: The EO Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (EO GSEA) is the premier event for student entrepreneurs worldwide. Student entrepreneurs compete against their peers from around the world in a series of local competitions to qualify for the EO GSEA Global Finals. EO GSEA is an Entrepreneurs’ Organization (EO) program. EO Mumbai chapter is bringing this opportunity to the student community in India. Structure: Application-based screening: The applications received will be filtered out on the basis of the information provided and the top shortlisted individuals will move ahead for the further rounds. EO Mumbai Finals: Shortlisted student entrepreneurs will be participating in the EO Mumbai Finals. Global Finals: All the Finalists from different clusters will then compete in the Global Finals for the ultimate battle. Prizes and Rewards: EO Mumbai Round: INR 5,75,000 EO Global Finals: USD 100,000 (plus a Paid International Trip for all finalists) Eligibility criterion to compete in the Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (GSEA): You must be enrolled for the current academic year in a university/college as an undergraduate or graduate student at the time of application. Full-time enrollment is not required; part-time enrollment is acceptable. You must be the owner, founder or controlling shareholder of your student business. Each company can be represented by only one owner/co-founder - studentpreneur. Your student business must have been in operation for at least six consecutive months prior to the application. Your business must have generated US $500 or received US $1000 in investments at the time of application. You should not have been one of the final round competitors from any previous year’s GSEA Global Finals Competition. The competitor must be 18-30 years of age. Note : Graduate students are eligible to apply only if they have continually enrolled in a university following their undergraduate degree and have not left school to work on their business or to seek other employment. Exceptions can be made for students who have taken up to one academic year off before beginning their postgraduate education.

title: Nexathon - Continuum 2027 Ideathon
organiser: Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology (MMMUT), Gorakhpur
description: Continuum 2027 Ideathon is an innovation and pitching challenge for students who can identify meaningful real-world problems and transform them into original, practical and scalable ideas . Participants will move from…
details_text: Continuum 2027 Ideathon is an innovation and pitching challenge for students who can identify meaningful real-world problems and transform them into original, practical and scalable ideas . Participants will move from problem identification → solution structuring → live pitching → jury Q&A . A working prototype is not mandatory . The focus is on the quality of the problem, originality of the solution, feasibility, impact, scalability and the ability to communicate and defend the idea. The Ideathon is part of CONTINUUM 2026 , the technical festival organised by NEXSUS at Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology, Gorakhpur . The festival brings together students, builders, problem-solvers and emerging-technology enthusiasts. Eligibility: Open to eligible college/university students. Participants from colleges/universities outside MMMUT may also participate. Individual and team participation may be permitted as per the final registration configuration. Only registered participants/teams will be considered for the competition. Competition Format Stage 1 — Problem & Idea Identify a meaningful real-world problem and define a focused solution. Ideas may address technology, sustainability, education, healthcare, mobility, finance, social impact, campus innovation, business/process innovation or other relevant domains. Stage 2 — Structure the Solution Develop a concise pitch covering: Problem statement Target users/stakeholders Key insight Proposed solution Innovation/originality Implementation approach Feasibility Expected impact Scalability/sustainability Stage 3 — Live Pitch & Q&A Teams present their idea before the jury at MMMUT, followed by a Q&A session. Participants must be able to defend their assumptions, solution choices, feasibility and expected impact. Evaluation — 100 Marks Criterion Marks Problem Understanding & Relevance 15 Innovation & Originality 25 Feasibility & Practicality 20 Impact & Value Creation 15 Scalability / Sustainability 10 Pitch Clarity & Communication 10 Response to Jury / Q&A 5 Total 100 AI & Originality Policy AI tools may be used for research, ideation, analysis, design and presentation preparation. However, participants remain responsible for the originality and accuracy of their submission and must understand and defend their major claims, assumptions and solution choices. Copied ideas, plagiarised presentations, false ownership claims or deliberate misrepresentation may result in penalty or disqualification. General Rules The idea must be original and meaningfully address a real problem. External research and existing products may be referenced for learning and comparison but must not be presented as the team's own work. Participants must follow the instructions of the organising team and jury. Jury decisions regarding evaluation and ranking will be final. Organisers reserve the right to disqualify submissions violating competition rules, originality requirements or participant conduct standards. Final event instructions, pitch duration and other operational details will be communicated by the organisers. Tagline: Turn a real problem into an idea worth building.

title: Pixel2Path 2027
description: Event Description: Pixel2Path is an autonomous robotics competition where teams build a robot that turns digital images into physical drawings on paper, with no human intervention. It combines Machine Learning, Computer…
details_text: Event Description: Pixel2Path is an autonomous robotics competition where teams build a robot that turns digital images into physical drawings on paper, with no human intervention. It combines Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Path Planning, Robotics, and Mechatronics. Online Submission: The teams have to submit the 'Documentation', 'BOM', and 'Video-Demonstration' of the bot. (Non-Eliminatory Round) Round 1 : The robot receives an unseen image (PNG/NPY), processes it, plans an optimized path, and draws it on an A3 sheet within the allotted time. Round 2 (Draw) : Each team gets an image with 40% of its strokes randomly removed. Their trained AI model predicts the missing strokes, and the robot draws the completed image (visible and predicted strokes) on A3 sheet. Round 2 (Predict) : Teams get 10 unseen masked images and predict the originals. Each is scored by SSIM. Teams get 100 image pairs two weeks before the event. On event day they get the full 5,000-pair dataset and a 60-minute window to train their model on Kaggle. Rules: Teams must have 3 to 5 members, with one designated Team Lead for official communication. Teams must bring a fully assembled and tested robot (no on-day mechanical builds), a laptop with all software pre-installed, the trained model weights file, a 12V DC power supply, and a USB cable for Arduino. It must be a 3-axis plotter (X, Y, and a Z pen-lift) with independent control of each axis. The robot must have an Emergency Kill Switch that completely stops all motion. Training must be done in a Kaggle Notebook on event day with GPU acceleration, with Internet toggled OFF. Training must be from scratch, using only the provided 5,000-image dataset. Data augmentation is allowed.

Presentation & Communication – Clarity, organization, confidence, and effectiveness of the presentation. Q&A Handling – Ability to justify recommendations, respond to questions, and demonstrate a thorough understanding of the case. details_text: goSTOPS Marketing Case Study – The Road Less Booked ₹30,000 prize pool | Internship opportunities | Real-world marketing challenge What would it take to get young travellers to book a place they wouldn't normally consider? At goSTOPS, we're tackling two real business challenges: driving demand for a mountain-view hostel outside Kasol's main market, and turning Alibaug into a more accessible destination for budget travellers beyond the weekend. In The Road Less Booked , you get to choose one of these challenges and build a marketing strategy around it. The challenge Option 1: goSTOPS Kasol PLUS The property is located outside Kasol's main market, away from the route most travellers typically follow. How would you turn its offbeat location and mountain views into a reason to book? Option 2: goSTOPS Alibaug Alibaug is often seen as a destination for villa stays and premium weekend trips. How can goSTOPS make it more appealing to budget-conscious young travellers, especially from Monday to Friday? Choose one property and build your solution around its specific business problem. What you'll work on This isn't just a campaign-ideas exercise. Your solution should be grounded in consumer behaviour and practical business thinking. Consumer research: Survey young travellers aged 20–35 to understand their travel preferences, barriers, brand awareness and stay choices. Present your key insight. Marketing strategy: Define your priority audience, positioning, channels and scalable marketing ideas, supported by a campaign cost breakdown. Campaign execution: Develop a campaign concept and show 2–3 sample executions across your chosen channels. We want to see original thinking, real consumer insights and ideas that could work in the real world. Who should participate? If you're interested in marketing, brand strategy, consumer behaviour, travel, growth or business problem-solving, this is your opportunity to put those skills to work. Team size: 1–3 members Format: Online Registration deadline: 30 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST Rewards A total prize pool of ₹30,000, along with internship opportunities. Refer to the official competition details for confirmed reward terms and eligibility. Ready to take on the challenge? Choose your property, understand the traveller, and build a strategy that gets them to take The Road Less Booked. Register on Unstop before 30 November 2026. At goSTOPS, we believe that some of the best ideas come from people who are willing to question the obvious, look at problems differently, and turn challenges into opportunities. Through this case competition, participants will get a chance to showcase exactly that — their ability to think critically, collaborate effectively, and build solutions that are both creative and practical. Bring your ideas. Bring your curiosity. Bring your problem-solving mindset and get ready to see how far you can take your solution!

details_text: About the event: Building India Case Study Competition is the largest undergraduate case study competition in India engaging students to solve challenging governance problem statements on Education, Sports, Public Health etc. Selected students get the opportunity to present their solutions in front of subject matter experts and government stakeholders. The theme of the fourth edition is "Substance Use". The problem statement is “How can India strengthen demand-side interventions to prevent and reduce substance use among youth by 2030?" Eligibility: Participants should be currently enrolled in an undergraduate program in India . Participants are required to submit a scanned copy of their college ID at every round of the competition for verification purposes. Participation in teams of two is mandatory. Both members must be from the same college, and individual participation is not permitted. Cross-specialisation and cross-year teams are permitted. Each student is allowed to be a member of only one team . Theme & Problem Statement The theme of the fourth edition is Substance Use, focusing on the need to prevent and reduce substance use among India’s youth. The problem statement, “How can India strengthen demand-side interventions to prevent and reduce substance use among youth by 2030?”, invites participants to explore practical, evidence-based solutions that address the underlying factors influencing substance use, including peer pressure, family environments, social norms and gaps in access to support. Participants are expected to develop implementable and scalable approaches that strengthen prevention, encourage early intervention, mobilise communities and leverage existing institutional mechanisms to create healthier environments for young people. Note: Participants who qualify for the Round 2: Idea Pitch Submission will be given a detailed case booklet to guide them in their solution submission. Process: 1. Registration (9th October 2026 - 1st December 2026) Registration details can be completed by the team leader but team member's consent will be required to complete the registration. Note: Any deviation from the aforementioned guidelines will result in the immediate disqualification of the team. Additionally, English will be the primary language for all communications and assessments. 2. Online Quiz (5th - 6th December 2026) Format: Registered teams will receive login details for the Online Quiz via their registered email address. The quiz will be conducted in a Multiple Choice Questions (MCQ) format. Teams will be tested on their general awareness, knowledge of current events, and understanding of the competition theme. Correct answers will earn the team 2 point each. There will be no negative marking for incorrect attempt(s). The Team Leader is designated as the primary member who is eligible to take the quiz. Results and Next Steps: The top-performing teams will qualify for the next stage. The result will be published on the website . Qualified teams will be notified via their registered email addresses. Qualified teams will receive detailed instructions about the requirements for the subsequent stage of the competition. 3. Idea-Pitch Submission (10th December 2026 - 3rd January 2027) Format: The qualifying teams will develop their solutions to the given problem statement on the theme of Substance Use in form of a 5-slide PowerPoint presentation in PDF format and a 3-minute video pitch and submit it by 03 January 2027 . PGPSM brings together management foundations, venture building, founder led learning, AI and emerging technologies, and hands-on startup immersion. Students learn by building and testing ideas, solving real startup problems, and making decisions in uncertain environments while learning directly from faculty, founders, and practitioners. details_text: About the Competition In today’s digital-first professional world, your online presence is becoming as important as your resume . A strong personal brand can help you get noticed, build credibility, connect with the right people, and create opportunities even before you formally apply for them. Platforms like LinkedIn and Instagram are no longer just social media platforms . LinkedIn has become a powerful space for professional networking, recruitment, thought leadership, and career opportunities, while Instagram has evolved into an important platform for personal branding, content creation, community building, and showcasing your personality, skills, and interests. Your resume may get you a foot in the door, but your digital presence can determine whether people remember you, trust you, and want to connect with you. Whether you are a student looking for internships, a fresher searching for your first opportunity, or a professional building industry connections, having a strong and authentic personal brand can significantly strengthen your professional journey. LinkedIn Launchpad is designed to help participants understand the importance of social media in today's professional ecosystem and express ideas, build credibility, and express your POV. The competition will challenge you to think about real-world issues, form your own opinions, and communicate those opinions effectively through LinkedIn. It is not just about what you think - it is about how you communicate, how you present, and how effectively you can build your professional voice online. Make sure you join the competition group for further updates and instructions. Write their response in a manner suitable for a professional LinkedIn audience. Publish/repost their written response on LinkedIn as instructed. Demonstrate their ability to communicate ideas clearly, creatively, and professionally. The objective is not simply to write about a topic, but to demonstrate how effectively you can form an opinion, communicate it, and create meaningful professional content that contributes to your personal brand. Submission Guidelines Individual participation only. All content must be original and based on the participant's own thoughts and perspectives. Responses must maintain professional and respectful language. Participants must repost the given problem on LinkedIn along with their own thoughts and perspectives, as instructed. Judging Criteria Participants will be judged on the quality and originality of their thoughts, creativity, clarity of communication, relevance of their perspective, professional presentation, and overall effectiveness of their content and personal branding. Exclusive Master Session Series by InteractUp , specially designed to enhance soft skills, worth ₹9,400 . Special LinkedIn Growth Paid Group access worth ₹2,100 , provided completely free. Total benefits worth ₹20,200 per participant, with a total prize value of ₹5,05,000 for the Top 25 participants. Important Note This competition is created purely for educational and professional development purposes. It aims to encourage participants to develop their professional voice, personal brand, and digital presence , understand real-world issues, and effectively leverage platforms such as LinkedIn and Instagram for networking, career growth, content creation, and professional opportunities. description: Overview: Reimagining the Education System invites you to rethink how people learn. In 250–400 words, identify one problem in education and propose a specific change that could make learning more meaningful, accessible,…
details_text: Overview: Reimagining the Education System invites you to rethink how people learn. In 250–400 words, identify one problem in education and propose a specific change that could make learning more meaningful, accessible, or effective. Explain why the change matters and how it could work in practice. This is a written-only challenge; no slides, photographs, or videos are needed. Who Can Enter: Everyone. No age, student, location, or cubing requirement. Individual entries only; entry is free. One entry per person. Submission: Enter an original 250–400-word response through the Unstop submission round by 31 Dec 2026, 11:59 PM IST. Give it a short title. The word count excludes the title. Keep a copy of your work. Rules: Your response must be your own. Do not submit plagiarised or AI-generated writing. You may cite outside ideas briefly, but clearly credit the source; do not copy passages. Avoid personal information about children or other people without permission. AceCubing may verify originality and disqualify entries for duplicate submissions or rule breaches based on evidence. Judging (100 Points): Problem insight and relevance: 25 Originality of idea: 25 Practicality and potential impact: 25 Clarity and strength of explanation: 25 Eligible entries are ranked by total score. If scores tie, compare originality, then practicality; if still tied, the rank is shared. Recognition: First place receives a ₹2,200 AceCubing gift card. Second place receives a ₹1,000 AceCubing gift card. Third place receives a ₹750 AceCubing gift card. These are gift-card face values, not cash payouts. Ranks 1–3 receive winner certificates. All other valid participants receive participation certificates. If a shared prize rank remains after tie-breaks, each tied participant receives that rank’s full gift card. Results will be announced after 31 Dec 2026, following verification. FAQs: Do I need to be a student? No. Can I submit a group entry? No, individual entries only. Can I submit a video or slides? No, written responses only. Is there a fee? No. Can I enter other Q4 challenges? Yes, each has its own registration and rules.

details_text: BRICS 2026: The De-Dollarization Summit A Pan-India Diplomatic Simulation What happens when the world's emerging economies come together to reshape the global financial order? Step into the world of international diplomacy, economics and strategic decision-making with BRICS 2026: The De-Dollarization Summit , a pan-India mock BRICS competition designed to test your understanding of global affairs while putting your negotiation, public speaking, strategy and teamwork skills to the ultimate test. Participants from across India will come together and be divided into teams representing different BRICS member countries. Each participant/ team will be assigned a country and will be expected to research its economic interests, geopolitical priorities and international position over the given agenda. The teams will then enter a simulated BRICS summit where they will negotiate, collaborate, debate and defend their country's interests around one central idea: Can BRICS reshape the global financial system through de-dollarization? Teams will be required to negotiate and work towards a common agenda or action plan that addresses the central issue. The summit will conclude with the teams attempting to reach consensus and pass a final resolution with the required majority of participating countries. This isn't just a debate. It is a simulation of international diplomacy where every decision, alliance and negotiation can influence the final outcome. We will also conduct one networking track so that all participants can connect with each other and make new friends and connections. What Will You Do? Represent a BRICS member country and understand your country's economic and geopolitical interests Develop a position on de-dollarization and negotiate with other countries Build strategic alliances/Defend your country's interests Participate in diplomatic discussions and negotiations and Present your final strategy and proposed framework Respond to challenges and developments introduced during the simulation What Skills Will You Test? Go beyond textbooks and experience how geopolitics, economics and diplomacy come together in the real world. Develop your strategic thinking, negotiation, research, public speaking and leadership skills while representing a country and making high-stakes decisions. Walk away with a deeper understanding of international relations, global finance and diplomatic decision-making, along with practical experience in teamwork, persuasion and problem-solving. Why Participate? Because this is more than a conventional competition; it is a global competition, where you compete with partipants from different geographies and challenge yourself to upscale. You won't simply answer questions or prepare a presentation. You will step into the role of a country and experience how international diplomacy actually works. Whether you are passionate about economics, finance, international relations, public policy, geopolitics, debating or simply looking for an intellectually engaging experience, this competition gives you a platform to think, negotiate, strategize and lead . Who Can Participate? The competition is open to students and young professionals from across India. Competition Format Round 1 - Country Allocation & Research Participants will be grouped into teams and assigned different BRICS countries. Teams will research their country's economic interests, foreign policy priorities and position on de-dollarization. Round 2 - The BRICS Summit The teams will participate in the mock BRICS summit, engaging in negotiations, diplomatic discussions, strategic alliances and formal presentations. Teams will present and defend their proposed framework for the future of the global financial system, followed by evaluation from the judging panel. The Final Question If the global financial system is changing, what role will BRICS play in shaping what comes next? Come prepared to represent. Negotiate. Strategize. Lead. title: Custom Paper Bags: How Small Brands Can Get Better Packaging
description: Custom Paper Bags That Make Sense for Growing Brands: Custom paper bags should work for your product, your customers, and your budget. Whether you're selling candles at a local market, shipping beauty products, or…
details_text: Custom Paper Bags That Make Sense for Growing Brands: Custom paper bags should work for your product, your customers, and your budget. Whether you're selling candles at a local market, shipping beauty products, or preparing for retail shelves, the right bag can make your brand feel more considered without forcing you into an expensive packaging order. The Cheapest Bag Isn't Always the Smartest Choice: Generic paper bags cost less upfront, but they can leave your branding looking disconnected. A coffee shop with premium products and a thin, poorly printed bag sends a mixed message. That doesn't mean you need luxury finishes. You need the right balance of paper quality, size, handles, and printing. Before ordering, check: Does the bag support the actual product weight? Is the size right, or are you paying to ship space? Will the print match your approved brand colors? Can the supplier handle your order quantity without surprise charges? I've seen small brands order thousands of bags before testing one with their actual products. That's an easy mistake to avoid. Choose Paper Bags That Fit Your Selling Channel: Your packaging needs change depending on where customers receive the product. A boutique beauty brand may need sturdy bags with twisted paper handles. A candle company should consider the weight and shape of glass jars. A retail brand preparing for store shelves needs consistent sizing and printing across different product lines. Keep Your First Order Manageable: Here's what actually works for early-stage brands: start with a quantity you can reasonably use, then scale when demand becomes predictable. Alora Packaging: Supports this approach with low MOQs, free design support, and free structural samples. That gives founders room to test a bag before committing to a large production run. No die or plate charges also help avoid costs that weren't part of the original budget. Alora Packaging has shipped for more than 10,000 brands, but the practical lesson is simple: get the size right, test the strength, and make sure the final cost works for your business. If you're planning a new bag order, start with your product dimensions and budget. A quick conversation with Alora Packaging can help you figure out what makes sense before you commit.

description: Mandatory Registration at: techfest.org/competitions/thetashift ThetaShift is a high-octane robotics challenge held as part of Techfest 2026-27 . Participants must design and construct a manually controlled, wireless…
details_text: Mandatory Registration at: techfest.org/competitions/thetashift ThetaShift is a high-octane robotics challenge held as part of Techfest 2026-27 . Participants must design and construct a manually controlled, wireless spherical robot built to navigate dynamic terrain, clear precision-based obstacles, and handle surprise course features . The top 5 teams from the Zonals round will qualify for the Grand Finale at the IIT Bombay campus from December 16–18, 2026 Key Rules & Technical Specifications: Bot Dimensions & Drive: Must be a wireless spherical bot with a diameter between 4 and 10 inches . Control Mechanism: Controlled manually via a joystick/remote or a mobile phone using 2.4GHz WiFi or Bluetooth . SSID format must follow TeamName_TF . Power Constraints: Onboard power supply only (≤ 24V DC for electric setups) . A physical power-disconnect switch is mandatory . Build Constraints: No ready-made Lego parts (ready-made gear assemblies permitted) . Spikes, abrasive materials, or adhesives damaging the track cause immediate disqualification . Arena & Challenge Breakdown: The 3x3m arena features 12 distinct terrain obstacles designed to test control, traction, and task execution : Terra Firma: Rock and sand path (50 Points) The Slalom Ridge: Triangular zig-zag barriers (30 Points) Sawtooth Ridge: Contiguous triangular speed bumps (30 Points) Infinity Circuit: Figure-8 path (60 Points) Domino Planks: Unevenly spaced rectangular planks (40 Points) Incline Overdrive: 10-degree incline ramp (40 Points) The Razor’s Edge: Elevated 7-inch wide track without side barriers (60 Points) Freefall Hairpin: Downhill slope ending in an immediate 90-degree turn (70 Points) The Gridlock: Alternating block grid path (30 Points) The U-Turn: Strict U-turn maneuver (20 Points) Bulldozer Drive: Pushing a block across a line and exiting in reverse (50 Points) Surprise Obstacles: Confidential obstacles introduced during the Grand Finale . Gameplay, Scoring & Time Limit: Time Limit: 6 minutes (360 seconds) per run . Each team gets 1 run . Scoring Formula: $\text{Total Score} = A + T - P$ A: Task Points earned (Max 480 Points) T: Time Bonus = 240 - Time in seconds (for runs under 4 minutes; Max 100 Points) P: Penalties (10 points per arena violation or extra pause time) Pauses & Resets: Two 45-second and one 30-second technical pauses allowed . Off-track bots reset to the start of the current obstacle with a 10-point penalty . Timeline & Rewards: Grand Finale: December 16–18, 2026 at IIT Bombay Campus . Certificates: Certificates of Excellence for the top 5 teams per zonal city and top 3 finale winners . Participation E-Certificates for teams crossing the benchmark score .

details_text: The International Conference on AI-Driven Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICAIDIET'26) is a premier global conference organized by SNS College of Technology, Coimbatore, in academic collaboration with Yorkville University, Canada. Papers not meeting the formatting or ethical requirements may be rejected without review. Final publication is subject to successful peer review, registration, and publisher quality checks. Submission Process Prepare your manuscript according to the conference guidelines. Submit your paper through the Microsoft CMT submission portal. Papers will undergo double-blind peer review by domain experts. Accepted authors will receive acceptance notification. Complete registration within the specified timeline. Submit the camera-ready manuscript. Present your work during ICAIDIET'26 in online or offline mode. Important Dates Paper Submission Deadline: 21 September 2026 (The submission deadline may be extended at the discretion of the Organizing Committee based on conference requirements and other relevant factors. Any extension will be announced through the official conference website and communication channels.) Acceptance Notification: 20 October 2026 Early Bird Registration: 22 October 2026 Late Registration: 23–28 October 2026 Final Manuscript Notification: 2 November 2026 Conference Dates: 20–21 November 2026 Publication Accepted and registered papers will be considered for publication in the Wiley Conference Proceedings, with submission for Scopus indexing, subject to publisher policies and indexing requirements. Join ICAIDIET'26 to showcase your research, interact with leading experts, build global collaborations, and contribute to the future of AI-driven engineering and technology. title: One Day workshop on Advanced Ensemble Learning Techniques for Supervised Machine Learning using Python 2026
description: This Workshop aims at providing a forum for members of the research and academy community. The Workshop enables the participants to understand the recent technologies in ML Foundations, ensemble techniques such as…
details_text: This Workshop aims at providing a forum for members of the research and academy community. The Workshop enables the participants to understand the recent technologies in ML Foundations, ensemble techniques such as Boosting, Voting, and Stacking, along with their practical implementation using Python. The One-Day Workshop on Advanced Ensemble Learning Techniques for Supervised Machine Learning aims to provide participants with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental concepts, advanced methodologies, and practical applications of ensemble learning. The workshop will introduce the principles of ensemble modeling and explain how combining multiple base learners can enhance the accuracy and reliability of predictive models. Participants will explore major ensemble techniques, including Bagging, Random Forest, Boosting, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Voting Classifiers, and Stacking.The workshop will emphasize the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of these techniques, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and suitability for different supervised learning tasks. Participants will gain insights into model selection, hyperparameter tuning, feature importance analysis, and performance evaluation using appropriate metrics for classification and regression problems. A hands-on session using Python and machine learning libraries such as Scikit-learn will enable participants to implement ensemble algorithms, experiment with real-world datasets, and compare the performance of individual models with ensemble-based approaches.

description: Biomedical optics has become one of the most inevitable field in the recent research in clinical diagnosis and treatment. In this course, we will learn about the fundamentals of biomedical optics, starting from how the…
details_text: Biomedical optics has become one of the most inevitable field in the recent research in clinical diagnosis and treatment. In this course, we will learn about the fundamentals of biomedical optics, starting from how the photon interacts with a single atom, to a diatomic species, and then with polyatomic species such as haemoglobin. You will learn the basics of spectroscopy and different imaging modalities such as fluorescence, UV-Vis-NIR, diffuse optics, polarization, Speckle contrast, and multimodal imaging. You will also learn about fundamental and advances in the field of optical biosensors and various plasmonic resonances. We will also discuss the principles and details along with demonstration of various microscopic imaging such as brightfield, phase contrast, fluorescence and polarization-based microscopy.The Department of Electronics and Communication, IIITDM Kancheepuram is organizing the 4th Edition of Winter School on Biomedical Optics (WiSBO ’26-27) at IIITDM Kancheepuram-Chennai, India between 27th December to 30th December. The participants (about 40 to 50) will be PhD students, Faculty members, and Industry participants working in the field of biomedical optics throughout India.

details_text: RAINSAT-2027 aims to bring together leading scientists, engineers, academicians, industrial researchers, and students from around the world to exchange ideas and discuss the latest advances in nanoscience and nanotechnology. RAINSAT-2027 will feature plenary lectures by internationally renowned scientists, keynote talks, invited lectures, contributed oral presentations, poster sessions, and industry interactions. The conference will encompass a broad spectrum of emerging topics, including nanomaterials, bio-nano interfaces, energy materials, soft matter, advanced characterization, computational nanoscience, sensors, environmental nanotechnology, and nanomedicine. The conference will be hosted by Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology, one of India's leading private deemed-to-be universities, recognized for its excellence in education, research, innovation, and international collaborations in science and engineering. We warmly invite researchers, faculty members, students, and professionals from across the globe to join us in Chennai for an exciting and intellectually stimulating scientific gathering.
